Grosvenor currently has the opportunity for up to eight interns to join our team for a five-week summer internship programme.
The internship, which will start early July, is based in our Central London office. Candidates on the programme will have the opportunity to work with one of the teams within Grosvenor to develop their commercial acumen, understanding of Grosvenor and of the wider real estate sector in a supportive, innovative and inclusive environment.
During the internship the successful candidate will:
• Spend time with one of our business teams to understand strategy, activities and priorities.
• Work independently on a variety of tasks and activities to support the team. This could include financial analysis, data modelling, reviewing documents, conducting research and/or assisting with the preparation and management of reports and papers.
• Attending meetings with members of the team to get an insight into their roles and remits.
• Learn more about Real Estate and the Grosvenor business through a programme of talks, presentations and location tours.
• Complete an assigned project during the internship and present their thoughts and findings.
This paid internship is open to those who are in their penultimate or final year of study, or who have already graduated. Interns on the programme in Summer 2027 will be offered the opportunity to apply for a graduate role, with successful candidates starting in September 2028. Applicants must therefore be available to start the two-year Grosvenor Graduate Programme in September 2028, should they be successful in securing a graduate role.
The Grosvenor Graduate Programme offers a great start to your professional life within property. Graduates on the programme will have the opportunity to work across some of the UKs best real estate and spaces.
Key Requirements
• Commercially minded, with a genuine interest in real estate and finance, and enthusiasm for developing an understanding of how financial analysis supports investment and business decisions.
• Grosvenor is a very collaborative business, so strong communication skills are a must. The successful candidate will be required to communicate and work with others both within their team and across the wider business.
• Ability to use own initiative and be effective at problem solving. Being organised and proactive are a must, as well as the ability to multi-task.
• Strong numerical and analytical skills. Comfortable working with data and information to inform thinking.
• Growth mindset, curious with enthusiasm for learning.
• Comfortable using a variety of IT and software packages (e.g: Excel, Powerpoint) and/or able to pick these up quickly.
• Demonstrates resilience and adaptability in changing environments
• Shares the Grosvenor values - Integrity, Respect and Trust.
This opportunity is based at the Grosvenor office at 70 Grosvenor Street, London W1K3JP.
Please note the application deadline of midday on 23 October 2026.
For further information on the opportunity and some FAQ's please see our website here.
We want you to have every opportunity to show us your strengths. There are adjustments available for our process, please contact us on grosvenor.recruitment@grosvenor.com to discuss.

It’s an exciting time to join the Technology team at Cancer Research UK (CRUK), our teams are now aligned to product portfolios ensuring we can deliver the best digital products and solutions to enable our pioneering work on how to prevent, diagnose, and treat cancer.
We’re searching for a Senior Full Stack Software Engineer who can take our digital products to the next level by partnering with our product teams to develop our software packages, and high-quality code; ensure best practice, and deliver technical solutions. In this role, you will be looking after two product portfolios.
If you have experience with TypeScript/JavaScript, AWS, and PHP and wish to be part of our journey in curing all cancers, please apply here.
Want to know more? Check out our candidate pack.
What will I be doing?
•
Delivering specific packages of development for software applications within our Science & Information (SIC) and Corporate Operations (COO) product teams, and running these applications in production.
•
Applying Lean and Agile principles to develop high-quality code that has minimal bugs, adheres to CRUK standards, and is highly supportable
•
Working either independently or in collaboration with Solution Architects to design new solutions in line with the Software Engineering strategy.
•
Working autonomously to deliver backlog items for an existing product.
•
Work in collaboration with Product Managers, Service Designers, UX Designers, Business Analysts etc to identify user needs, discuss capabilities and iteratively design solutions
•
Supporting the development of more junior software engineers through mentoring
What we’re looking for
Essential
•
Experienced Software Engineer with experience in TypeScript/JavaScript, AWS, PHP
•
Ability to write clean, readable, and properly tested code based on tried and tested design patterns.
•
Ability and willingness to learn new languages, frameworks and tools.
•
Experience building modern user interfaces and single page applications using the React/NextJS ecosystem.  Experience developing APIs and other back-end components using Node.js and PHP
•
Experience in acting as a technical lead in a team, starting the development of new features from scratch, defining the overall solution, and reviewing more junior engineers’ work
Desirable
•
Some experience with cloud-native architecture and AWS services, various SQL and noSQL databases, as well as queues such as SQS
•
Some experience in running critical services in production and designing highly-available, scalable and secure solutions
What will I gain?
Without you, we wouldn’t be able to achieve our aim of seeing 3 in 4 people survive cancer by 2034. So, we want to reward you in as many ways as possible. Our benefits package includes:
•
Flexible working - office-based 1 or 2 days a week on average
•
25 days holiday + bank holidays + 1 CRUK day (option to buy up to 5 days per annum).
•
Stratford Olympic Park location (Less than 10-minute walk to National Rail, Jubilee, Central, and Elizabeth lines; Westfield Shopping Centre, Queen Elizabeth Olympic Park, Gym…)
•
Pension (employer contributions up to 10%).
•
Life insurance.
•
Brilliant learning and development opportunities.
•
Discounts – Westfield Shopping Centre, travel, technology, gym memberships, and much more…
If you’re as ambitious as we are, join our collective force and enjoy an excellent career, as we save and extend lives then apply here!
Cancer Research UK’s Technology team is proud to be part of the Tech Talent Charter (TTC) for our efforts in driving equality, diversity, and inclusion in the workplace. Our vision is a digital world accessible to all, and we have always sought to draw from a diverse pool of talent and maintain an inclusive working environment.
At CRUK we value diversity and we're committed to creating an inclusive culture where everyone is able to be themselves and to reach their full potential. The Living Sector Finance team sits within the Structured Finance Office for EMEA and is responsible for the origination, structuring and execution of Real Estate Finance transactions across the UK and Europe.

• A proactive, investigative and critical-thinking mindset, with sound judgement and the ability to test assumptions, distinguish symptoms from root causes and challenge information constructively.

Desirable

This is an exciting opportunity to work in the Connexions team with SEND young people to support their transition into adulthood from school into further education, training and employment.
You will have a caseload targeting year 11 SEND young people in school settings including special schools, pupil referral units, alternative provision and also Post 16 NEETs.
If the postholder requires a Standard or Enhanced DBS disclosure the candidate is required to declare full details of everything on their criminal record unless the conviction/s and/or caution/s are considered “protected” in line with filtering rules for DBS checks.
For an informal discussion about the role, please contact Fiona Arnott, on 07718 100 818 or Fiona.arnott@hullcc.gov.uk
ROLE AND PURPOSE
The purpose is to work with young people with an Education Health and Care Plan from age 14 – 25 to support their transition into adulthood with particular emphasis on education, training and employment outcomes including supported internships and inclusive apprenticeships. The role will contribute to the Preparation for Adulthood strategy by improving outcomes for SEND learners, ensuring accurate data is reported to internal and external stakeholders including DfE, and informing proposals to cease EHCPs. This will be delivered through impartial information advice and guidance in a range of locations including schools and other venues both internal and external to Hull City Council.
The post holder will help to develop and promote SEND employability by working with stakeholders including young people, parent/carers, DWP, education and training providers, third sector organisations and the business community to ensure SEND young people have access to a full range of opportunities to meet their needs and aspirations. The postholder will also develop strong links with Children’s and Adult’s social care and Hull City Council’s SEND team to support the transition of SEND young people into sustained Education Employment and Training.
As well as post 16 young people with an EHCP the post holder will hold a caseload of young people in Hull special schools and/or Alternative Providers and will support those identified as being at risk of becoming NEET to transition into suitable post 16 provision. This will assist with the Councils statutory responsibility regarding ‘Participation’ in education and NEET reduction for this vulnerable group of young people.
Using data from sources which include post 16 education and training providers, the SEND team and adult social care, the postholder will track and maintain information on the current situation of individual young adults in the cohort to better identify those who are NEET or not known.
The postholder will also contribute to the organisation of events promoting SEND employability including the annual SEND Post 16 Options and PFA event, information events promoting supported internships and Reverse Job Fairs for SEND young people to showcase their skills to employers.
You will make a positive contribution to the wider Preparation for Adulthood by supporting transitions and raising aspirations for young adults with an EHCP. You will also help to inform the timeliness of proposals to cease the EHCP.
PRINCIPAL ACCOUNTABILITIES:
1.    To promote and safeguard the welfare of children, young people and/or vulnerable adults.
2.    Statutory Obligations –
Makes a positive contribution to the preparation for adulthood agenda particularly supporting and encouraging the achievement of education, training and employability outcomes for young adults with an EHCP and reducing the number of NEETs and not knowns in the cohort. Champions equality of opportunity for young people with SEND.
3.    Maintains effective records utilising the Client Caseload Information System to ensure reporting to DfE and KHCC is accurate, comprehensive and timely. Maintains and manages own caseload to follow-up and track young adults with an EHCP from 16+ through lists of “not known”, “currency lapsed”, “risk of NEET” and “NEET” young people to ensure that data is current and that support is timely.
4.    Assesses the individual’s current situation and readiness to progress, using appropriate tools, such as career guidance databases, and techniques, evaluates the information and feeds this back in order to identify and agree next steps. Uses specialist knowledge to decide and make appropriate referrals to other agencies and professionals including Adult Social Care.
5.    Establishes and maintains effective relationships with young adults on their caseload in order to support them effectively including challenging the individuals’ current attitude to employment, education and training where appropriate.
6.    Has in depth specialist knowledge of the local labour market and education and training opportunities including supported internships and inclusive apprenticeships and knowledge of packages to promote reasonable adjustment such as the health adjustment passport, Access to Work funding and Better off in Work calculator to advocate on behalf of individuals, raise aspiration and support progression.
7.    Attends relevant meetings where a young adult’s future options are being discussed in order to support transition, preparation for adulthood and provide specialist advice to the individual, their parents/carers and other professionals, for example at EHCP annual reviews.
8.    Has an awareness of the barriers relating to transition into adulthood and advocates on behalf of individuals. Can support young adults with SEND in seeking appropriate provision. Making applications and preparing them for interviews and selection processes.
9.    Works effectively in partnership with other professionals including the SEND team, adult social care and health. Develops and shares specialist knowledge base on a regular basis with team members and partners from within the organisation and external stakeholders.
10.    The Health and Safety at Work etc. Act 1974 and associated legislation places responsibilities for health and safety on Hull City Council, as your employer and you as an employee of the council. In addition to the Councils overall duties, the post holder has personal responsibility for their own health, safety and wellbeing and that of other employees; additional and more specific responsibilities are identified in the Council’s Corporate H&S policy.

At our 64,000 sq ft Bishops Cleeve facility in Cheltenham, our teams deliver predominantly electronic and electro-mechanical product lines, specialising in fuel measurement systems, emergency oxygen systems, barometrics and complex electro-mechanical assemblies.
As Ontic continues to grow, so does the importance of having strong financial foundations behind our operations. We’re looking for an ambitious Financial Controller to lead the financial accounting and control activities for our Bishops Cleeve site.

You’ll be responsible for the accuracy, integrity and timeliness of financial reporting at Bishops Cleeve, while continually looking for opportunities to strengthen controls, simplify processes and improve the way we work.
Your responsibilities will include:
• Leading the month-end close, ensuring an accurate and timely period close in line with finance policies, procedures and the month-end checklist.
• Reviewing, approving and posting journals and ensuring appropriate supporting evidence and controls are in place.
• Taking ownership of Balance Sheet integrity, ensuring reconciliations are robust, supported and completed to the required standard, while introducing new reconciliations as the business evolves.
• Ensuring accounting standards and internal and external controls are consistently applied throughout month-end reporting.
• Acting as the site's Controls Champion, owning and developing the financial control framework and ensuring continued adherence to established controls.

• Helping develop a control environment capable of supporting a growing organisation, including readiness for potentially enhanced or SOX-style controls in the future.
• Leading site cash management, including forecasting operating cash performance and providing effective reporting and insight.
• Using systems, data and technology to identify efficiencies and improve the month-end close process and timetable.
• Leading the site's relationship with external auditors, coordinating the audit process, providing high-quality audit trails and ensuring queries are resolved effectively.
• Overseeing VAT and Fixed Assets activities.
• Preparing and submitting annual insurance data requirements.
• Reviewing and approving payments.
• Managing, supporting and developing a Financial Accountant.
• Working closely with colleagues across Finance, Operations and Ontic's wider global finance community, including our US teams.
What you’ll bring
You’ll combine strong technical accounting knowledge with the confidence to take ownership, challenge existing ways of working and turn ideas into practical improvements.
We’re looking for someone who has:
• A recognised professional accounting qualification, such as ACCA or CIMA.
• Strong financial accounting, reporting and control experience.
• Experience of US GAAP would be advantageous.
• Strong systems capability and advanced Excel skills.
• A continuous-improvement mindset, with an interest in using data and technology to make finance processes better.
• The ability to communicate financial information clearly and confidently to both finance and non-finance audiences.
• Strong relationship-building skills and the ability to work effectively across different functions and levels of the organisation.
• The confidence to embrace and support change in a fast-moving, growing business.
• The ability to prioritise effectively, work under pressure and deliver against demanding deadlines.
• The leadership skills to coach and develop others while maintaining high standards of financial discipline.

This is more than a role focused on producing the numbers.
You’ll have the opportunity to influence how the financial control environment develops as Ontic grows, strengthening the processes, systems and disciplines that underpin reliable decision-making.
You’ll work closely with Finance leadership, operational teams and global stakeholders, giving you broad exposure across the business and the opportunity to make a visible impact at one of Ontic’s key UK sites.
Benefits
At Ontic, we care about your financial, physical and mental wellbeing. Our benefits are designed to support what matters to you, alongside a culture built around recognition, empowerment and a healthy work/life balance.

A bit about us
Big opportunities. Personal support. That’s Beyond the Ordinary.
Want to spend six weeks building experience that could take your career further? Our Summer Internship gives you the chance to learn by doing, work with clients and build experience alongside people who’ll support you as you go. BDO is the largest organisation in the UK mid-market and the only one above £1bn in revenue, with 8,000 people across the UK. That gives you the scale, expertise and breadth of opportunity of a major professional services organisation, alongside the personal support and close relationships that make BDO beyond the ordinary.
The programme starts on Monday 5th July with an organisation-wide induction in Coventry (fully paid for). During this one-week induction, you’ll get an introduction to BDO, our values and our service lines.
You’ll then be based in the office you applied to for the rest of the programme. You must be able to commit to the full six-week duration.
A bit about Audit
In Audit, you’ll get an inside look at how different organisations work and the role Audit plays in providing financial information that businesses and their stakeholders can trust.
BDO’s Audit teams work across specialist areas including Pension Audit, Public Sector, Not-for-Profit, Financial Services and Technology Risk Assurance.
During your internship, you’ll get hands-on experience working with clients, while learning how our teams assess risks, challenge judgements and understand the systems behind financial statements. With BDO looking after over 400 of the UK’s 6,000 pension schemes, you’ll get exposure to work at significant scale and see how Audit supports organisations across different sectors.
You won’t just be watching from the sidelines. You’ll have opportunities to contribute to live work, learn directly from experienced colleagues and start building your problem-solving, commercial and relationship skills.

And a bit about the programme
During your internship, you’ll explore our business areas, learn about professional qualifications and take part in workshops focused on our values, culture and wellbeing. Then you’ll put that learning into practice, getting involved alongside experienced colleagues and other interns.
It’s a chance to try new things, build your confidence and get a proper feel for working at BDO – with people around you to answer questions and help you make the most of the experience.
As for you
You’re inquisitive, adaptable and ready to learn. You enjoy solving problems, working with other people and trying something new.
You don’t need to arrive knowing everything about Audit. Bring your curiosity and willingness to get involved, and we’ll give you opportunities to build your skills, confidence and experience from there.
Join us in one of the following hubs - Birmingham, Edinburgh, Glasgow, Leeds, Liverpool, London, Manchester, Nottingham, Reading or Southampton.
One thing to note: you’ll need to live within a commutable distance of the office you apply to. Relocation support is not provided, so please consider this carefully before applying. Time together in person matters – whether that’s in the office or with clients – for your learning, building relationships and getting the most from your internship.

Please note: we do not use UCAS points. You’ll be asked to provide evidence if you’re successful in securing an offer
• GCSEs at grade 4 and above in Maths and English, or Scottish National 5 grade A-C. You’ll also need to provide evidence if successful
• The right to work in the UK

We want you to know what to expect, so here’s the typical process:
• Online application form.
• Online assessments.
• Video interview.
• Virtual assessment centre and interview.

Our benefits are designed to support your life in and outside of work, with options including additional leave, gym membership and employee discounts, alongside pension, health and wellbeing support and a range of protection benefits.

£26,615 - £28,275 depending on location

You’ll have opportunities to get involved, with people around to help you learn and make the most of them.

Job Description
Senior / Lead FPGA Engineer
Wotton under Edge
Salary from ~£45,000 - £65,000 depending on experience
We have multiple opportunities for ambitious FPGA Engineers at Senior and Lead level to join our multidisciplinary engineering team at the forefront of additive manufacturing technology.
Our FPGA platforms are central to the control, sensing, communication and real-time processing capabilities of our next-generation products. Working within Research & Development, you will contribute to the full product lifecycle, from concept and architecture through verification, release to production, and long-term support.
These are hands-on engineering roles, combining FPGA design, verification and hardware bring-up with close collaboration across electronics, software, systems, algorithms and mechanical engineering teams. Depending on experience and grade, you will also provide technical leadership, influence engineering strategy, and mentor developing engineers.
The FPGA frequently interfaces with high-speed digital electronics, embedded processors, sensors and analogue circuitry. As such, a strong appreciation of system-level design and hardware/software interaction is essential.

FPGA Design & Development
•
Develop FPGA architectures and RTL designs from concept through to production release.
•
Design, implement and maintain high-quality VHDL solutions with a focus on performance, reliability, portability and efficient resource utilisation.
•
Perform timing analysis, constraint development, timing closure and design optimisation.
•
Implement and verify FPGA functionality in both simulation and on target hardware.
•
Develop reusable and maintainable IP blocks and design frameworks for use across multiple projects and product generations.
•
Support product sustainment, issue investigation and design improvements throughout the product lifecycle.
Verification & Validation
•
Develop robust verification environments using modern methodologies including OSVVM and VUnit.
•
Create reusable, self-checking testbenches with measurable verification coverage.
•
Define verification strategies, plans and acceptance criteria.
•
Drive continuous improvement in simulation, regression testing and automated verification workflows.
•
Support hardware validation, debugging and system integration activities.
Systems & Product Development
•
Capture, analyse and refine requirements, ensuring clear traceability from customer and system requirements through to implementation and verification.
•
Work closely with systems, electronics, software, algorithms and test engineers to deliver integrated solutions.
•
Evaluate and implement signal processing, control and embedded algorithms within FPGA architectures.
•
Contribute to safety, reliability and compliance activities, including design assurance and audit-ready engineering evidence.
•
Produce and maintain high-quality technical documentation, including architecture specifications, interface definitions, verification reports and design rationale.
Technical Leadership
•
Provide technical leadership for FPGA development activities across projects.
•
Drive engineering excellence through design reviews, code reviews, development standards and best practices.
•
Support planning, estimation, technical risk management and project delivery.
•
Mentor engineers, graduates and apprentices, helping develop both technical capability and engineering judgement.
•
Promote reusable design approaches and continuous improvement across tools, methodologies and processes.
Essential Requirements
Senior FPGA Engineer
•
Degree in Electronic Engineering, Physics, Computer Engineering or a related discipline.
•
Strong commercial experience developing FPGA solutions using VHDL.
•
Solid understanding of digital design principles, including:
•
Timing analysis and timing closure
•
Clock domain crossing techniques
•
Reset architectures
•
Pipelining and resource optimisation
•
High-speed digital interfaces
•
Experience implementing and verifying FPGA designs in simulation and on hardware.
•
Understanding of FPGA development tools and design flows.
•
Ability to communicate effectively within a multidisciplinary engineering team.
Additional Requirements for Lead FPGA Engineer
•
Significant experience architecting complex FPGA-based systems.
•

Network Engineer, Cyber Defence Centre
Alternatively, Grant Thornton
At Grant Thornton we do things differently - looking to the future, driving ambitious growth and pioneering positive change in our industry. Providing audit, tax and advisory services, we empower clients through strategic insight, curiosity, and genuine partnership. And we empower our people with real opportunity, an inclusive culture and work life balance. A true alternative.
With over 5,000 people in the UK, and a presence in 150 global markets, we're on an ambitious journey, from great to exceptional, and we need the best people to help us achieve our potential. And with that comes the opportunity to help redefine what our industry looks like, and what you want from your career.
About us
The Grant Thornton Cyber Defence Centre is an award-winning* managed security services provider operating at the forefront of cyber security, using industry-leading technologies to protect and support our clients. Alongside our SOC capability, we have cutting-edge incident response teams delivering rapid cyber breach investigations for clients through insurance panels and direct engagements, supporting organisations at their most critical moments.
We invest heavily in our people, offering clear progression opportunities and encouraging initiative within a collaborative, cross-functional environment with a strong team ethos. Support is always available across the SecOps, DFIR, MSS and wider cyber teams.
We’re seeking an experienced Network Engineer to join our Cyber Defence Centre. This is a hands-on technical role that spans live incident response, security assessment and hardening, and the design and delivery of managed security solutions in client environments. You will be one of the people clients rely on to shut an attacker out of their estate and then help make sure it does not happen again.
A look into the role
As a Network Engineer within the Cyber Defence Centre, you will deliver the containment and recovery phases of live client incidents, and work on assessment, hardening and implementation engagements between them.
Incident response, containment and recovery
• Delivering the containment and recovery phases of live client security incidents, including ransomware, business email compromise and perimeter device exploitation.
• Isolating affected systems and accounts, restricting compromised identities, closing off attacker access routes, and preventing further spread across the estate.
• Preserving logs and evidence for the forensic investigation team, and working alongside them as the investigation develops.
• Supporting client recovery, including rebuild and restoration sequencing driven by business priority, and ensuring known weaknesses are not reintroduced.
• Implementing the remediation and hardening work identified through the incident, where clients engage us to deliver it.
• Working to the NIST Cyber Security Framework and incident response lifecycle, with CIS Benchmarks used for technical control recommendations.
Security assessment and hardening
• Performing security reviews and configuration hardening across Microsoft 365 and Entra ID, Microsoft Azure, Amazon Web Services, on-premise Active Directory, and perimeter firewall estates.
• Conducting firewall security assessments across multiple vendor platforms: rule base review, management plane exposure, VPN and remote access configuration, IPS/IDS posture, logging, and firmware currency.
• Assessing cloud configuration against CIS Benchmarks and NIST using tooling including Prowler, ScubaGear and PingCastle, and turning technical findings into prioritised, business-contextualised remediation plans.
• Reviewing third-party software, cloud applications and SaaS platforms as part of supplier and technology assurance work.
• Supporting client compliance and assurance requirements including GDPR, Cyber Essentials Plus and PCI DSS.
Security solution design and implementation
• Designing and implementing security solutions in client environments, from discovery and requirements gathering through build, testing, rollout and handover.
• Working as part of the delivery team on a Zero Trust access programme built on Netskope One SASE, covering Secure Web Gateway, CASB (inline and API), Private Access (ZTNA) and Data Loss Prevention, integrated with Microsoft Entra ID and endpoint management.
• Designing and deploying Microsoft 365 conditional access policy sets, including MFA enforcement, legacy authentication blocking, device compliance conditions, geolocation restriction, and Privileged Identity Management for just-in-time privileged access.
• Designing network segmentation across cloud and on-premise environments: Azure Network Security Groups and subnet-level control, VLAN segregation, DMZ isolation, and layer 2 / layer 3 access control.
• Designing data classification and DLP policy, working with client data and business process owners to define label sets and handling outcomes, and validating policy behaviour in simulation before enforcement.
• Producing security architecture artefacts, hardening standards, deployment guides, operating procedures and SOC playbooks so client teams can operate and extend what you have built.
Knowing you’re right for us
Joining us as an experienced Network Engineer, the minimum criteria you’ll need is a background in network engineering with demonstrable experience of applying it to security outcomes, ideally with 36 months in a security-focused role, together with the Netskope Certified Cloud Security Integrator (NCCSI), which you must be actively working towards if you do not already hold it. You should also be able to demonstrate the following during the interview process.
Technical experience
• Networking: LAN/WAN, VLAN segmentation, layer 2 / layer 3 access control, routing and switching, DMZ architecture, DNS and DHCP. A background as a network engineer prior to moving into security.
• Network security: Cisco (including Firepower), Palo Alto, FortiGate, SonicWall, Check Point, WatchGuard, Sophos, Zyxel and F5. Firewall policy design and review, IPS/IDS, site-to-site and remote access VPN, and SSL/TLS inspection.
• SASE and Zero Trust: Netskope One, Secure Web Gateway, CASB, Private Access…

Job Description:
Start date: September 2027
Location: Broughton
Duration: 36 months
Application: We love your interest in joining Airbus! There is no limit on the number of positions you can apply for, however, please be aware that you can only progress in the selection process for one position at a time. We recommend reviewing all available opportunities and applying to those that best match your experience and aspirations.
Closing date for applications: 15th December 2026
Benefits
Salary: A competitive starting salary of £19,185
35 hours per week (on either a standard working day or a double-day shift pattern, providing flexibility) // 25 days holiday plus bank holidays // Pension // Success share // Plus many more flexible benefits!
About us:
Ready to build the wings that lift the world? Join Airbus as a Craft Machining Apprentice in Airbus Broughton and play a vital role in manufacturing wings for our A320, A330, and A350 aircraft families. This 36-month program offers valuable hands-on training, recognised qualifications, and a clear path to a rewarding career in aviation."
At Airbus, we believe a diverse workforce drives innovation. We're committed to fostering an inclusive environment where everyone feels valued and empowered to thrive.  Airbus is a global pioneer in the aerospace industry, leading the way in designing, manufacturing, and delivering aerospace products across Commercial Aircraft, Helicopters, Defence, and Space sectors. As the global center of excellence for wing manufacturing, our Broughton site delivers over 500 wing sets annually. Our apprenticeship programs are carefully designed to give you valuable practical training alongside your academic studies, setting you up for success and helping your career truly fly.
With over 17,5000 employees worldwide and as the largest aeronautics and space company in Europe, Airbus is at the forefront of the aviation industry. During your apprenticeship you will work alongside our experienced engineers and quality team to support you to complete the work safely and efficiently
What you will be doing:
As a Craft Machining Apprentice, you'll immerse yourself in hands-on technical experience in the workplace while completing your academic studies. This program is designed to equip you with valuable qualifications and competencies to work directly on live aircraft. You'll also benefit from our Gen A support network and learning HUB, providing additional support, events, and opportunities for all early career participants.
This 36-month apprenticeship is structured to maximise your learning and impact:
Year One: You will spend the first 12 months of your apprenticeship based at Coleg Cambria, Bersham Road, Wrexham, working towards obtaining:
• NVQ L2 diploma in Performing engineering operations
• City & Guild 2850 Level 2 In Machining
• Level 2 Essential Skills
This will allow you to develop the necessary skills, knowledge and experience to enable you to make an immediate contribution when you enter the workforce in the second year.
Year 2 and 3:  Your Learning Takes Flight at Broughton! Building on your foundational knowledge, you will be based at Airbus Broughton (North Wales) and you'll join our expert team of Machinists within the machine shop area, supporting the manufacture of wing skins, panels and stringers for various Airbus aircraft.  The tasks will be varied,  and will require you to apply your skills directly to live projects,  allowing you to work on the job whilst gaining the relevant skills, knowledge and experience. This will include:
• Carrying out a variety of different techniques including following bespoke set up sheet instructions to complete a machining process as well as the use of stringer machining and long bed milling machining practices within the Airbus Broughton plant, completing this to a high competent level and in a safe efficient manner.
• Through your training you will have the ability to demonstrate effective loading and locating of billets, and unloading of finished components within the Airbus Broughton plant, completing this to a high competent level and in a safe efficient manner.
Additionally you will also attend college on day release, working towards gaining:
• Level 3 Extended Diploma in Mechanical Manufacturing Engineering (Machining Bias Units)
• City & Guild 2850 Level 3 Machining
Upon successful completion of your 36-month apprenticeship, you'll become a skilled Machinist  working within the Large component manufacture (LCM) team supporting our world-class Airbus aircraft. You'll receive a Modern Apprenticeship Certificate, setting you up for a fantastic career.
Requirements
In order to be eligible to this apprenticeship you must:
• Achieve a minimum of five GCSEs which must include:
• Grade C or 4 in Maths (GCSE certificate only - no equivalency accepted)
• Grade C or 4 in English Language (GCSE certificate only - no equivalency accepted)
• Grade CC or 44 in Double Award Science OR Grade C/4 in Single award in Physics.
• Plus 2 other GCSEs at grade C or 4 (other qualifications that are equivalent or higher may be considered as an alternative to the additional 2 GCSE’s, preferably in a practical or technical subject (e.g., Design & Technology, Engineering, etc)
• Attach your CV (stating your predicted or achieved grades) and cover letter stating your motivation for the role and industry.
To be a successful candidate you need to have a passion for learning, enjoy hands-on, teamwork and problem-solving activities.
BOOST YOUR APPLICATION
We want to get to know you! Not just your grades or school background so, tell us on your cover letter:
• Why Airbus?
What is it about Airbus that makes you excited to start a career with us? Is it our aircraft, innovation, global impact, or something else? Let us know what interests you about our work and why we stand out to you.
• Why a hands-on apprenticeship?
Why do you want to learn by doing? We’d love to hear what draws you to practical, skills-based learning.
• Show your hands-on experience.
In your CV or cover letter, include any hands-on activities or hobbies where you've used practical skills. These could be things like:
• DIY projects
• Building and fixing things
• Doing make-up or beauty work
• Tinkering and Tech Projects
• Building models
• Baking or cooking
• Others
Important Information:
GRADES: Any offer will be conditional upon us receiving evidence of your required grades 24h after receiving your certificates on results day, in addition to completing all pre-employment checks and online forms.
SECURITY CLEARANCE: You will be subject to a BPSS (Baseline Personnel Security Standard) check. You may also need to gain UK SC-level Security Clearance or Export Control, depending on the role.
RIGHT TO WORK IN THE UK: Candidates must have current legal authorisation to work in the United Kingdom. For more information, please check the Government Website.

Thank you for asking! Kindness and curiosity are some of Atelier Ten’s core tenets.
We are a team of building services engineers and environmental designers championing for a healthier planet leveraging our vast, collective knowledge of sustainable spaces. We help bring elegance and efficiency to every building, and we work with architects, engineers, owners, and other stakeholders to accomplish their sustainable vision. What is this role on a high level?
We are seeking an exceptional leader to join Atelier Ten as Regional Director, MEP
Engineering UK. This is a business-critical leadership role responsible for driving the growth, performance, and strategic direction of our MEP practice across the UK, with teams based in London, Manchester, Glasgow, and Edinburgh.
As a client champion, team builder, and technical leader, you will play a pivotal role in expanding Atelier Ten's multidisciplinary offering, strengthening our presence in key markets, and growing a market-leading MEP team that complements our internationally recognised sustainability and environmental design expertise.
This role is about more than managing projects. You will be responsible for winning work, developing long-term client relationships, identifying new market opportunities, attracting and developing talent, and shaping the future direction of the business. You will work closely with fellow directors and practice leaders to grow our MEP capability, enhance our multidisciplinary offering, and deliver exceptional outcomes for clients across the UK and beyond. The position combines business development, operational leadership, people management, technical oversight, and strategic planning, making it an ideal opportunity for an entrepreneurial leader who thrives on building successful teams and growing businesses.
What your day-to-day looks like
No two days are the same. You will balance business leadership, client engagement, team development, and technical guidance while helping shape the future growth of Atelier Ten's engineering practice across the UK.

• Leading and implementing the growth strategy for the MEP business across the UK market.
• Building and maintaining strong relationships with developers, architects, asset owners, contractors, and industry partners.
• Driving business development activities, identifying opportunities, leading pursuits, and securing new projects.
• Acting as executive sponsor and director-in-charge on key client commissions.
• Providing technical leadership and oversight across major multidisciplinary projects.
• Growing, mentoring, and developing a high-performing MEP team.
• Collaborating closely with Atelier Ten's sustainability, environmental design, and specialist engineering practices.
• Supporting recruitment, succession planning, and capability development across the business.
• Leading resource planning, utilisation, and financial performance to ensure sustainable business growth.
• Representing Atelier Ten through industry events, conferences, thought leadership, and professional networks.
• Contributing to business strategy, operational planning, and the long-term growth of the practice.
• Engaging with other SJ Group companies, such as Robert Bird Group in London or the SJ MEP teams in the Middle East or Asia, on joint initiatives around business growth and technical development.
What we are looking for
Hopefully you’re interested and excited about what your days at Atelier Ten will look like. We do have a few items on our wish list for you to become the next great “ATenner”.
We’re looking for someone who is entrepreneurial, passionate about sustainable design, and has a knack for bringing in business. If you’re the kind of person people genuinely enjoy working with—someone who brings positive energy and builds trust—that’s even better! And if we’re not pushing our luck with asks, you will be a self-starter and ideally, you will bring:
• Proven leadership experience within building services or MEP engineering consultancy.
• A strong track record of leading and growing engineering teams.
• Established relationships across the UK property, developer, architect, contractor, and institutional sectors.
• Proven success in winning major projects and developing long-term client partnerships.
• Experience managing business performance, resources, and profitability.
• Strong leadership skills with a passion for mentoring and developing future talent.
• Chartered Engineer status and membership of a relevant professional institution.
• Deep technical expertise in building services engineering and sustainable design.
• Strong communication and presentation skills, with the ability to represent the business internally and externally and influence at senior levels.
• A collaborative leadership style and enthusiasm for working in a multidisciplinary environment.

Job Description:
Your impact
The 13-week Summer Industrial Placement Programme
Are you ready to make an impact and gain hands-on experience working on real-world projects from day one?
At Leonardo, we’re looking for summer placement students who want to be part of something extraordinary shaping innovation, advancing technology, and enhancing global safety.
Our placements are designed to help you apply your studies in a practical setting, develop your technical skills, and gain valuable insight into how our business operates.
We have created a programme across our UK sites that not only increases your technical skills, but gives you the opportunity to work on meaningful real-life projects, alongside experienced engineers and graduates across our business.
You will receive coaching and support to achieve your personal goals and work in multidisciplinary teams to gain as much experience across the product lifecycle from your time in industry as possible.  Our aim is to see you through your undergrad years and successful placements may result in an offer to return for further placements or for an offer on our Graduate Development programme.
This programme is remunerated £26,228 per annum.
The programme will run from 1st June- 27th August 2027
What you’ll do as a Summer Placement Systems Engineer
Systems Engineers are involved in all aspects of design and development; from initial product design through to in-service support.
They look at the big picture, determine how the system needs to operate and collaborate to produce the required overall operational behaviours. They also dive into the deepest level of detail – taking the system piece-by-piece and defining its design to the finest point. Our Systems Engineers can also actively engage in R&D, developing new concepts and conducting fundamental research into our  future technologies.
As a Summer Placement Systems Engineer, you will work on real engineering problems within either the Radar or the Advanced Targeting business area.
You will have the opportunity to be involved in supporting a wide range of tasks across multiple projects/products, such as:
• The radar for the Typhoon fighter jet
• The radar for the SAAB Gripen fighter
• Our family of Surveillance AESA (Active Electronically Scanned Array) radars
• An IRCM (Infra-Red Counter Measures) system
• Our laser target designator or laser ranging systems
Core activities within Systems Engineering include:
• Requirements capture, design documentation, verification and validation.
• Algorithm design and test.
• Performance modelling; building physics-based models to test our designs through computer simulation.
• Data analysis; end-to-end systems analysis using synthetic and ‘real world’ data.
• Applied research; from product improvements to blue-sky thinking.
You will work with an experienced engineer who will provide day-to-day guidance and on-the-job training. You will be introduced to systems engineering processes, methods, technology and tools, with particular emphasis placed on learning practical skills that may not be easily gained or experienced in the academic environment of a university.
What you’ll bring
• Be a self-motivated individual, willing to take on new challenges and drive continuous personal development
• Strong communication skills across a variety of mediums i.e. written, verbal, digital, etc.
• The ability to develop effective working relationships with peers and stakeholders
• Adaptable to the ever-changing demands that will be encountered within the role
• Offer novel ideas and methods for solving technical problems, drawing on personal experiences and knowledge learned during academic studies
Role Requirements
All of our Summer Placement roles require you to be currently studying a relevant degree discipline such as Physics, Mathematics, Engineering, or other STEM subject degrees. This should be a minimum of a Bachelors level degree.
All successful candidates must be returning to university after their Summer Placement, i.e. not in their final year.
In addition to this, we would be interested in hearing from you if you have experience in:
• Coding/programming.
• Relevant project work and/or placements in industry.
• Applying your science and technology knowledge to solve a real-world problem
This is not an exhaustive list, and we are keen to hear from you even if you might not have experience in all the above. The most important skill is a good attitude and willingness to learn.
Security Clearance
At Leonardo, many of our roles are subject to security and export control restrictions set by UK Government Security requirements and customer obligations.  As a result, and in line with the UK Government Baseline Personnel Security Standard (BPSS) requirements, all successful applicants will be asked to provide evidence of identity, eligibility to work in the UK, criminal record declaration information and employment and/or education history verification for the previous five years.
For staff operating in more sensitive posts, there is an additional range of personnel security controls referred to as National Security Vetting (NSV).  As part of this process, a range of factors may be considered, including an individual's background, travel history, nationality, previous nationalities held and other information relevant to the vetting assessment.
To be eligible for National Security Vetting at SC level, applicants will generally be expected to have continuously resided in the UK for the previous five years. For DV clearance, this is typically ten years.  In some circumstances, time spent overseas may be accepted, with additional overseas checks.  Additional vetting requirements may apply upon appointment.
For more information and guidance please visit: https://careers.uk.leonardo.com/gb/en/security-and-vetting
Why join us
At Leonardo, our people are at the heart of everything we do, key contributors in shaping innovation, advancing technology, and enhancing global safety.
We offer a comprehensive benefits package that supports your wellbeing, learning and development, and work–life balance:
• Time to recharge: Our employees are entitled 25 days of annual leave plus bank holidays. As a Summer Placement student you will receive this allowance pro rata.
• Secure your future: Award-winning pension scheme with up to 15% employer contribution
• Your wellbeing matters: Free access to mental health support, financial advice, and employee-led networks championing inclusion and diversity (Enable, Pride, Equalise, Armed Forces, Carers, Wellbeing and Ethnicity)
• Never stop learning: Free access to 4,000+ online courses via Coursera and LinkedIn learning.
For a full list of our company benefits please visit: https://careers.uk.leonardo.com/gb/en/company-benefits

Job Description:
Grant Thornton’s Alternative Funds tax team provides tax advisory, transactions and compliance services to alternative fund managers across all asset classes including private equity, venture capital, private debt, hedge funds, real estate and infrastructure.
The team’s client portfolio spans the breadth of the asset management sector, serving traditional asset managers, financial services institutions, private equity funds, alternative investors, the real estate sector, wealth and hedge asset managers, UK pension funds, and global institutional investors. We combine technical expertise with a commercial approach, to build a strong trusted adviser relationship with our clients.
The Alternative Funds tax team sits as part of the wider Financial Services Tax team, which provides tax services to a variety of clients in the Financial Services market across Wealth and Asset Management, Banking and Capital Market and Insurance sectors.
We have ambitious growth plans and are looking for an experienced, enthusiastic Associate Director with strong UK tax compliance and advisory experience to join our team in London. The alternative funds industry is dynamic, technically demanding and global, giving you the opportunity to work on domestic and international structuring, transactions and UK tax compliance and advisory matters, in addition to working with the wider Grant Thornton International network.
You will be responsible for managing the full suite of tax compliance and advisory services for asset managers themselves and the funds they manage, across the entire investment lifecycle including fund structuring, structuring carried interest arrangements, structuring the investment and divestment of assets and ongoing tax compliance and investor reporting.
Part of the role will focus on working alongside the partner group in building out the practice, building strong client relationships within the current and target client base. Working in practice means that the job is, by its nature, different every day and we want someone who is actively looking for this challenge. An agile approach to working with different projects and people is therefore essential.
We’re happy to talk flexible working and consider reduced hours and job shares, we’ll support you to balance your work and life.
A look into the role
As an Associate Director you will:
•
Take ownership of providing highly technical tax advice to asset managers and the funds they manage throughout the investment lifecycle of the fund, including transaction and tax structuring support
•
Deliver partnership tax and corporate tax compliance services to asset management businesses, ensuring their tax reporting obligations and compliance deadlines are met
•
Assist with investor reporting to enable clients to effectively communicate taxable results to their individual investors
•
Develop and lead your own diverse client portfolio, ensuring a high level of client service
•
Work closely with our colleagues cross the Grant Thornton’s tax practice, Financial Services Industry and international network to identify opportunities from both new and existing clients
•
Actively contribute to business development activities by proactively managing existing relationships and pitching work to new clients
•
Proactively train and develop more junior members of the team, including through the delivery of bespoke training sessions
•
Have a thorough understanding and adhere to the firm’s risk management and quality procedures
Knowing you’re right for us
Joining us as an Associate Director the minimum criteria you’ll need is a professional qualification (CTA / ACA / ACCA or equivalent), and to be confident managing a portfolio of clients.
It would be great if you also had some of the following skills, but don’t worry if you don’t tick every box, we’ll help you develop along the way.
•
Strong tax technical skills and an interest in the financial services sector (previous experience of working with one of the asset classes (private equity, venture capital, private credit) is preferred but is not essential
•
Mix of corporate and partnership tax compliance experience
•
A track record of leading projects, with a focus on accountability, high quality and timely delivery.
•
Self-motivated and strong team player.
•
Excellent interpersonal skills are required in addition to strong oral and written communication skills.
•
Familiarity with Alpha tax, CCH personal tax, Power BI, Microsoft Office, and other relevant software.
•
Experience of coaching and developing more junior team members.
Knowing we’re right for you
Embracing uniqueness, the culture at Grant Thornton thrives on the contributions of all our people, we never settle for what is easy, we look beyond to deliver the right thing, for everyone.  Building an inclusive culture, where we value difference and respect our colleagues helps our people to perform at the best of their ability and realise their potential.
Our open and accessible culture means you’ll interact with leaders who are interested in you and everything you bring to our firm. The things that set you apart, we value them. That’s why we give you the freedom to bring your whole self to work and pursue your passions inside and outside of work.
Beyond the job
Life is more than work. The things you do, and the people you’re with outside of work matter, that’s why we’re happy to look at flexible working options for all our roles, and we’ll always do our best to keep your work and life in balance.
The impact you can make here will go far beyond your day job. From secondments, to fundraising for local charities, or investing in entrepreneurs in the developing world, you’ll be giving back to society.  It’s that drive to do the right thing that runs through our every move, grounded in our firm’s values – purposefully driven, actively curious and candid but kind.
We’re looking for people who want to contribute, spark fresh ideas and go beyond expectations. People who want to be able to proudly do what’s right, for the firm, our clients, our people and themselves. It’s how it should be.

Locations: DL, DH, NE, SR, TS
Are you a qualified Dual Fuel Smart Meter Engineer looking for excellent earning potential, structured work and the security of working directly for an established energy supplier?
At Utilita, we're growing our award-winning Field Services team. Join one of the UK's fastest-growing energy suppliers and a business that has been recognised as one of the UK's Top 50 Best Workplaces for four consecutive years.
What is in it for you?
You'll receive a base salary of £38,993, alongside uncapped earning potential and a variety of opportunities to boost your overall earnings, including:
• On-call payment: Receive £330 for each on-call week, based on an average rota of one week in five. (OTE of £42,293 just with the base salary and conducting mandatory on call requirements)
• Industry-leading installation bonus: Benefit from an uncapped installation bonus of £25 per meter or £50 per dual installation once you have completed a minimum of four installations in a day, with additional work opportunities available to further enhance your earnings.
• London weighting: Receive an additional £2,000 annual allowance if you live within the M25.
• Enhanced overtime: Enhanced overtime rates for Sunday working.
Alongside your salary and uncapped earning potential, you will receive 25 days’ annual leave plus bank holidays, a healthcare scheme, mental wellbeing support, access to 24/7 GP and counselling services, and a generous pension scheme. You will also receive one paid volunteering day each year and have opportunities to win tickets to events at Utilita-sponsored arenas and football matches.
Why work at Utilita?
A schedule that supports your work-life balance.
We understand that a great Smart Meter Engineer role is not just about salary. It is also about having a structured working day and being able to plan your life accordingly.
You will be scheduled an average of 4 jobs per day, with an average travel time to jobs of approximately 35 minutes between appointments.
We aim to schedule your work several weeks in advance, giving you greater visibility of your schedule. This helps you plan life outside work while still giving you the opportunity to take on additional work when it suits you.
First-class training and support.
Your journey will begin at our award-winning training academy in Warrington, where you will receive a comprehensive induction.
You will then receive ongoing mentoring to help you strengthen your knowledge, understand our processes and confidently adapt to the Utilita way of working.
A team that keeps you connected.
We understand that working in the field can sometimes feel isolating, which is why creating a connected and supportive environment is so important to us.
Through regular manager check-ins, access to technical experts, collaborative colleague networks and ongoing communication, you'll always have the support you need and someone to turn to throughout your working day.
What you will be doing.
As a Dual Fuel Smart Meter Engineer, you will represent Utilita in customers’ homes, installing smart meters safely and professionally across domestic properties.
You will play an important role in delivering our customer-first approach, providing a positive experience while maintaining high standards of safety, quality and service.
What we need from you.
To be considered for this opportunity, you will need:
• Smart Metering qualifications, including CCN1 or CMA1 and MET1, or equivalent.
• At least 12 months experience working as a Dual Fuel Smart Meter Engineer.
• A valid full UK driving licence.
Who are Utilita?
Founded in 2003, Utilita Energy was created to challenge the Big Six energy suppliers by offering a fair and flexible service that is good for both the pocket and the planet.
As the first supplier to install a Smart Meter back in 2005 and kick-start Britain’s smart meter revolution, we continue to invest in smart technology and look for new ways to improve our services through innovation.
We are also committed to sustainability, with an ambition to become a Net Zero business by 2030. We believe everyone can make a meaningful impact through small, positive changes.
Our values are simple but powerful:
Fairness. Smart. Sustainability.
Our employees and customers come from all walks of life. We are committed to championing diversity, creating an inclusive culture and providing an environment where you can be your authentic self.
Utilita is part of the Luxion group which comprises Luxion Group Ltd, Utilita Energy Ltd, Luxion Sales Ltd, Utilita Field Services Ltd, Procode Technology Ltd and Canary Care Global Ltd.

Senior Compensation Specialist – Pay Equity and Transparency
The Senior Compensation Specialist provides specialist support to the Senior Compensation Manager – Pay Equity and Transparency, helping ensure Flutter remains compliant with global pay legislation and delivers clear, consistent pay equity reporting and communications. Working closely with the Compensation Data & Analytics team, the role helps ensure pay equity analysis is set up and run correctly, but its primary focus is translating those data outputs into clear findings, and findings and partnering with regional Reward teams and People Partners to agree and track appropriate actions. The role also provides broader ad-hoc support to the wider team as required.
What you’ll do:
• Pay equity analysis & audits: Partner with the Data & Analytics team to quality-check pay equity models, translate outputs into clear findings for stakeholders, prepare audit documentation, and work with regional Reward teams and People Partners to agree and track follow-up actions.

• Communications & training: Draft employee- and manager-facing guides on pay equity and transparency, and help coordinate and deliver related training sessions.
• Stakeholder support & BAU implementation: Act as first point of contact for pay equity queries, support practical implementation of processes, and provide day-to-day cover on routine matters in the Senior Compensation Manager's absence.
• Data governance & reporting: Maintain accurate records, audit trails, and version control; support development of KPIs and reporting packs; and collaborate with the Data Automation & Analytics team on compliant data collection.
• Broader project & team support: Contribute to project documentation, status reporting, and meeting coordination; assist with procurement/vendor records, leadership materials, and other Reward BAU cycles (e.g. benchmarking, job architecture); and bring curiosity to AI/automation initiatives that improve analysis and reporting.
How you’ll do it:
• Pay equity & compliance knowledge: Working knowledge of pay equity/transparency concepts and international legislation (e.g. EU Pay Transparency Directive), plus data privacy considerations for employee data.
• Data interpretation: Skilled at translating compensation/pay equity data outputs into clear, actionable findings, partnering with analytics specialists rather than building analyses independently.
• Stakeholder partnering: Proven experience working with regional/divisional Reward teams and People Partners to agree and track actions from data or compliance reviews.
• Compensation frameworks: Solid understanding of job architecture, job evaluation, and pay benchmarking principles.
• Documentation & audit support: Experience maintaining accurate trackers, records, and documentation to support audit and compliance needs.
• Communication & training: Ability to develop clear communication and training materials for diverse stakeholder audiences.
• Systems familiarity: Exposure to HRIS platforms (e.g. Workday) and pay equity/compensation software desirable.
• Personal attributes: Detail-oriented, analytical, collaborative, adaptable, and professional when handling sensitive data, with strong self-motivation and prioritisation skills.
What’s in it for you:
We are a flexible employer. If you have personal commitments or a hobby that brings happiness, we want you to bring your best self to work and feel empowered to do so. We also like to share our success since you make it happen. We offer an excellent benefits package that can be personalised to you:
• Bonus scheme
• Uncapped holiday allowance
• Enhanced pension scheme
• Private healthcare
• Life assurance
• Income protection
• £1,000 annual self-development learning fund
• Invest via the Flutter Sharesave Scheme
• Enhanced parental leave

Flutter Entertainment is the world’s leading online sports betting and gaming company, operating some of the most innovative, diverse, and distinctive brands in the sector. takeaway.wd3.myworkdayjobs.com/jet-ecs-r.description_excerpt:
Ready for a challenge?
Then Just Eat Takeaway.com might be the place for you. We’re a leading global online delivery platform, and our vision is to empower everyday convenience.
Whether it’s a Friday-night feast, a post-gym poke bowl, or grabbing some groceries, our tech platform connects tens of millions of customers with hundreds of thousands of restaurant, grocery and convenience partners across the globe.
About this role
As Senior Supply Chain Analyst, you will provide the independent analytical layer behind every major planning decision across our global supply chain. This is not an operational planning role — it's strategic and project-focused, centred on validation, performance analytics, reporting, and process improvement.
You'll build and maintain dashboards in Anaplan and AI tools that power our key planning and performance meetings, work closely with the Demand Planning Analyst to build the monthly performance narrative, and deep dive into the drivers behind underperformance by product category and by market — covering packaging, equipment, marketing goods, and devices.
The function influences approximately €40m annual spend. Your analysis will directly inform decisions that protect courier equipment availability, ensure device availability for restaurant partner launches, and safeguard the supply chain's contribution to business growth.
These are some of the key components to the position:
•
Independent validation: Review critical forecasts, inventory plans and major proposals. Escalate risks, keep plans data-led and lead root cause analysis.
•
Performance dashboards: Lead AI innovation across the supply chain. Build and maintain dashboards using our ERP system and AI tools.
•
Planning system partnership: Work with internal stakeholders to keep the planning environment as the single source of truth, brief in requirements, validate data integrity and shape new data views and outputs.
•
Deep dive analysis: Investigate what's driving performance by country, product and stakeholder. Surface root causes behind forecast misses, consumption variances and inventory deviations, and track overstock and slow movers.
•
Monthly review and storytelling: Partner with the supply planning team to build a clear, action-driving narrative for monthly performance and execution reviews. Support key stakeholder meetings with easy-to-digest data showing performance against KPIs.
•
Stakeholder bridge: Translate supply chain methodology and performance into language that Finance, Marketing, Operations and country teams can act on.
•
Process improvement and AI: Own monthly and quarterly reporting and lead initiatives that cut manual workload, increase automation and improve data quality across planning systems and AI tool integration.
What will you bring to the team?
•
Experience: Degree in Supply Chain, Logistics, Business, Finance, or related field. 3+ years in supply chain analytics, planning, or a closely related analytical role.
•
Analytical Rigour: Ability to interrogate large datasets, identify root causes — not surface-level reporting — and present findings clearly.
•
Anaplan & Dashboards: Experience with supply chain planning systems (Anaplan preferred). Track record of building performance reporting and dashboards for senior stakeholders.
•
Data & Tools: Advanced Excel. Experience with AI tools (Claude, ChatGPT, or similar) for business analytics is a plus.
•
Storytelling: Can turn complex supply chain data into a clear narrative that non-experts can follow and act on. Knows their audience and tailors accordingly.
•
Independent Challenger: Willing to provide objective, data-led challenge to planning decisions. Proactive problem-solver who brings solutions, not just observations.
•
Supply Chain Knowledge: Understanding of demand planning, supply planning, and inventory management principles. MCIPS/CIPS qualification is desirable.
At JET, this is how we play
Our teams forge connections internally and work with some of the best-known brands on the planet, giving us truly international impact in a dynamic environment.
Being the best at what we do isn’t just about delivering on our strategy. It's a competition for something incredibly valuable – our customers' choice. Every time a customer decides where to order, they're picking a side.
At the heart of the JET Customer League are our values and behaviours. They guide every interaction, every decision, every innovation. These are the actions we need to perform consistently and brilliantly to surpass the competition and earn our customers’ loyalty, again and again.
Fun, fast-paced and supportive, the JET culture is about movement, growth, helping one another to succeed and celebrating wins. By truly living our values and embodying our behaviours, we’re building a customer-first culture which enables us to stay one step ahead of the competition.
Inclusion, Diversity & Belonging
No matter who you are, what you look like, who you love, or where you are from, you can find your place at Just Eat Takeaway.com. We’re committed to creating an inclusive culture, encouraging diversity of people and thinking, in which all employees feel they truly belong and can bring their most colourful selves to work every day.
What else is cooking?
Want to know more about our JETers, culture or company? Have a look at our career site where you can find people's stories, blogs, podcasts and more JET morsels.
Are you ready to take your seat? Apply now!

Location: Bristol — Semtech Bristol Design Centre (Bradley Stoke, United Kingdom)
Hybrid Working: Monday–Thursday Onsite (Friday Flexible)
Our Team:
Most test engineers get handed a test plan. In this role, you’d be the one writing it — not for a single device, but for entire product platforms.
Our Global Test Engineering team is the technical backbone behind every product in Semtech’s semiconductor portfolio, working across design, product engineering and offshore manufacturing partners to make sure silicon is fully characterised, robustly tested, and production-ready at scale.
This is a technical leadership seat, not an execution-only role — the strategies and standards you set here ripple out across significant product lines, not just a single project.
Job Summary:
We’re looking for a Staff Test Engineer with deep Advantest V93000 expertise to support test strategy and architecture for significant product lines and technology platforms.
This isn’t about running a test plan someone else designed — you’ll be the one setting the test coverage objectives, building the methodologies, and deciding how the whole organisation approaches test for the platforms under your remit.
You’ll lead complex test program development, drive statistical and adaptive test methods, own test-based yield and quality initiatives, and set the technology roadmap for the test platforms you’re responsible for — all while mentoring engineers and representing test engineering in technical forums and reviews.
If you’ve got 5–7 years of progressive semiconductor test engineering experience on the Advantest V93000 platform and you’ve actually led test development initiatives — not just contributed to them — this is the seat where that leadership finally has a platform-wide remit.
Responsibilities:
Here’s what you’ll actually own, day to day:
• Develop and implement V93000-based test strategies and architectures for significant product lines or technology platforms, aligned to quality and business objectives
• Support and lead on complex test program development for advanced semiconductor devices, including sophisticated test algorithms and measurement techniques
• Implement statistical and adaptive test methods, and provide technical leadership on the hardest test development challenges
• Lead test optimisation initiatives — advanced data analysis, predictive models, and strategies that balance coverage, quality and cost
• Drive reductions in test time and improvements in throughput through continuous improvement of test methods and procedures
• Lead test technology and innovation initiatives, including next-generation test capabilities and technology roadmaps for test platforms
• Lead test-based yield and quality improvement programs, including sophisticated yield analysis, correlation methodologies and outlier detection
• Act as test engineering subject matter expert to product and manufacturing teams, and provide technical mentoring across the test engineering function
• Build collaborative relationships with design, quality and production engineering, and represent test engineering in technical forums and reviews
Minimum Qualifications:
• Bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, or a related technical field; Master’s degree preferred
• 5–7 years of progressive experience in semiconductor test engineering
• Experience leading test development initiatives and optimisation projects
• Advanced knowledge of semiconductor test methodologies, the Advantest V93000 platform, and data analysis techniques
• Experience in a semiconductor manufacturing environment required
• Comfortable with moderate travel (10–20% of time) across test facilities, manufacturing sites and customer locations
The Right Candidate Will Be Able To:
• Apply expert knowledge of semiconductor test principles, methodologies and technologies, including device physics, parametric testing and failure mechanisms
• Work confidently with test equipment capabilities, languages and programming techniques
• Apply statistical analysis, design of experiments and test optimisation techniques
• Lead test initiatives with strong project leadership, analytical and problem-solving skills
• Communicate and document technical decisions clearly, and think strategically to align test strategies with product objectives
• Draw on strong understanding of quality standards, reliability testing, product qualification and test data/yield analytics
Why Join Us?
• Set test strategy and standards for significant product lines — not just execute someone else’s plan
• Take on genuine technical authority — approve test specifications, shape methodology, and guide resource allocation
• Mentor the next generation of test engineers while staying hands-on with the hardest technical challenges in the function
• Get exposure across test facilities, manufacturing sites and customer locations — a genuinely global view of the business, not a desk-bound one
Career Growth Philosophy:
At Semtech, we value engineers who combine deep technical expertise with real organisational influence. This role is a direct route into principal and architect-level technical leadership, with the scope to shape test standards that the wider engineering organisation adopts.
Ready to Apply?
Engineers who can genuinely lead test strategy across an entire platform — not just execute one — are rare, and the ones who can also mentor a team and hold their own with customers and manufacturing partners are rarer still.
If that’s you, don’t wait for a bigger title to land somewhere else first. Apply today and let’s talk about which platform you’d take on.

Incumbents may be required to perform job-related tasks other than those specifically included in this description.
All duties and responsibilities are essential job functions and requirements and are subject to possible modification to reasonably accommodate individuals with disabilities.

About Waythrough
Waythrough provides specialist support across mental health, alcohol, drugs and related areas. We delivery high-quality, evidence-based services designed around the real needs of the people we serve.
Every year, we support around 125,000 people through over 250 services - and it's all made possible by our 3,500 brilliant staff and volunteers.
Make a real difference in your community
Are you passionate about helping others live safer, healthier, more independent lives? Join our team at Waythrough and support people facing challenges around mental health, substance use, housing or domestic abuse. This is more than just a job – it’s a chance to build meaningful relationships and create lasting change.

It provides a range of support, interventions and treatments for adults and young people wanting to make positive changes to their drug and/or alcohol use, as well as offering support to family members and running campaigns and events that raise awareness of addiction and celebrate recovery in the community.
Reading Through Recovery
A weekly 90‑minute group supporting anyone on a substance or alcohol recovery journey, whether actively using or abstinent, through the shared experience of reading.​
​
In a relaxed and inclusive space, participants bring a book they’re reading, explore themes that resonate, and dive into stories that spark insight and strength. Together, we share literature that has inspired, supported, or shaped our recovery journeys, with optional recommendations and themed reading ideas each week.​

This is more than a book group, it's a place to find meaning, connection, and momentum in recovery.​
