Studio Overview
We are Sports Interactive 🎮
The studio behind: ⚽ Football Manager.
Founded in 1994, Sports Interactive became a wholly owned subsidiary of SEGA Europe in 2006. Based at the Here East technology hub in Stratford, East London, the SI team continues to expand as we bring our titles to an ever-growing audience across an increasing variety of platforms.
To support our growth, we welcome the opportunity to connect with passionate people with the drive to match our ambitions and initiative to realise your individual potential.
Job Title: Senior Producer (Design)
Team: Design
Reporting into: Lead Producer
Working Model: Hybrid 2-3 days per week in Studio
Location: Here East, Queen Elizabeth Olympic Park, London, E15 2GW
Position Overview
​
We are hiring a Senior Design Producer to elevate and accelerate design delivery across Football Manager.
This role exists to bring assertive, pro-active ownership to the day-to-day execution of work across our UIUX, narrative, and game design teams (consisting of ~20 designers across multiple features & initiatives).
Following two challenging cycles we are looking for a highly organised, experienced producer who can ensure design work is clearly planned, communicated, and delivered predictably without compromising creative quality.
On an annual release cadence, it is imperative that design lead the way early and that work is not allowed to drift or delay development. You will be accountable for ensuring design work is delivered at pace and is ready to enter production. You will ensure that dependencies and risks are surfaced early, and progress tracked with clarity and intent.
Whilst you will primarily take ownership of day-to-day execution, as a senior member of the production group you will also help shape process, mentor producers, and act as a trusted partner to design and production leadership.
Key Responsibilities
•
Assertive accountability for delivery of UIUX, narrative, and game design output across multiple features and initiatives
•
Operate with urgency and efficiency in the context of an annual release cadence
•
Successfully position design to be delivering ahead of the next iteration, not reacting late
•
Partner with Design Leads to translate creative vision into achievable plans, timelines, and milestones
•
Proactively identify delivery risks, dependencies, capacity constraints, and mitigation strategies
•
Safeguard design quality through effective planning that considers stakeholder feedback and iteration loops
•
Ensure validation gates are utilised and requirements satisfied to enable designs to move into production with confidence
•
Drive build reviews and continuous improvement initiatives
•
Support evolution and improvement of design production processes to enable clarity, consistency, and scalability
•
Provide clear, concise, and actionable updates on progress, risks, and decisions
•
Facilitate alignment and collaboration across creative, technical, and production perspectives
Knowledge, Skills, and Experience
•
Proven experience in senior game production roles with accountability for delivery of creative work
•
Deep understanding of production in a creative setting, with experience delivering in a deadline-driven environment
•
Able to bring solid organisation and pro-active intent to a fast-moving, ambitious studio
•
Comfortable operating among legacy complexity whilst focussed on forward-thinking opportunity
•
Strong command of production tools (Jira, Confluence) with an understanding for how they add delivery confidence, not administrative overhead
•
A confident communicator with strong stakeholder management skills
•
Experience working on large-scale, systems-driven or simulation-heavy games
•
Familiarity with Football Manager or deep sports simulation titles
Benefits of Working at Sports Interactive:
•
Private Healthcare and Dental Plans.
•
A range of Gym Membership options through our Benefits partners.
•
Travel Insurance for yourself and your family.
•
Subsidised mental health, therapy, and coaching sessions are available.
•
Access to our on-site physical and massage therapist services.
•
Free access to games released under the SEGA Europe umbrella.
•
Contributory Pension Scheme (up to 7% of annual salary).
•
Regular events in collaboration with our partnered football clubs.
•
Free onsite evening bar in our London HQ.
•
A well-stocked breakfast bar with cereals, fruits, teas, and coffees.
•
Multiple clubs and societies to join e.g., book club and art workshops.
•
Your club’s shirt personalised upon passing probation.
•
Trophies & gift cards for length of service milestones.
•
Cupcakes delivered on your birthday.
What is it like to work here?
We approach everything with passion, whether that is making our mark on the football industries or doing our bit for the world around us. We want to share that outlook with everyone who shows up to work here each day.
For us, talent wins games, but teamwork wins titles. All our roles require a level of Studio attendance to help us collaborate effectively and stay connected as a team. Collaboration is the key to constantly topping our best. Everyone's contribution counts, no matter which part of the business you are in. We encourage and support our people in driving your own growth and realising your full potential. But, more than anything else, we are a team. A team with a down-to-earth dynamic, that has a lot of fun doing what we do.
And whether that’s technical tweaks or fine-tuning our creative process, everything is geared at producing the best game possible for our players. To do that, we need to be tenacious and ambitious and not be afraid of switching things up. It is these principles that have enabled us to produce a game that has defined year after year, and that will continue to push us for many more to come.
We’re also a London Living Wage employer and boast one of the lowest staff turnover rates in the industry.
We are proud to be an equal opportunities employer and encourage applications from any relevant candidate irrespective of sex, race, disability, age, sexual orientation, gender reassignment, marriage or civil partnership, pregnancy or maternity, religion, or belief.
SI is proudly a Disability Confident Committed employer, and we are dedicated to ensuring our recruitment process is inclusive and accessible. Our studio has disabled access and facilities but please ensure you advise us if you require any other reasonable adjustments to be made to support you during the recruitment process.
Our Values:
•
Keep collaborating: Teamwork wins titles - Here, ideas belong to everyone, whatever department you’re part of. Collaboration lets us score more as a team than we could individually.
•
Be flexible: We think fast and adapt faster. The football and entertainment worlds never stand still, so we keep progressing and switching things up to stay ahead.
•
Stay Tenacious: We don’t overlook the details. Everything we do is about producing the best game…

Group Director of Commercial Growth & Pricing
Location: Wallingford, Oxfordshire (or flexible within portfolio)

Role Overview
The Group Director of Commercial Growth & Pricing is the executive responsible for driving revenue expansion, pricing strategy, and commercial performance across Vesta’s portfolio companies. This leader will define and operationalise the commercial playbook for the group, bringing sophistication, consistency, and scalability to pricing, customer expansion, and revenue optimisation.
The Group Director of Commercial Growth & Pricing owns the commercial engine room — ensuring that every Vesta business maximises revenue, margin, and organic growth through world-class commercial discipline.
This role combines strategic thinking with hands-on execution, embedding commercial excellence in newly acquired companies and building a data-driven culture of pricing optimisation, upselling, and customer value creation.
Key Responsibilities
Commercial Growth Leadership
• Build and lead the group-wide Commercial Growth function, developing a high-performing team capable of supporting multiple business units.
• Define commercial growth frameworks covering customer segmentation, value-based selling, upsell/cross-sell design, and account expansion strategies.
• Partner with portfolio leaders to identify organic revenue opportunities and turn them into executable, measurable growth programs.
• Introduce commercial performance dashboards, playbooks, and benchmarks used consistently across the group.
Pricing Strategy & Execution
• Own the group’s pricing strategy, ensuring pricing models are modern, data-driven, and aligned to value creation.
• Lead the strategic pricing reviews for all acquisitions and core businesses, identifying margin opportunities and pricing improvements.
• Develop dynamic pricing models, discount frameworks, and monetisation strategies that improve profitability.
• Embed pricing governance to ensure consistency across contracts and markets
Portfolio Support & Commercial Excellence
• Conduct commercial health checks for each business to assess pricing maturity, sales process, packaging, and product-market fit.
• Deploy targeted interventions where businesses are under-performing commercially.
• Support leaders with strategic bids, contract renewals, competitive positioning, and customer value propositions.
• Facilitate commercial training, best-practice sharing, and capability uplift across the portfolio.
Data, Insights & Performance Measurement
• Implement commercial analytics, including CAC, LTV, price-realisation, churn, retention, and cohort analysis.
• Establish KPIs and reporting that allow the Group CEO and board to track commercial progress across all units.
• Ensure decisions are based on robust data, market research, competitive analysis, and customer insights.
Qualifications & Experience
• Proven senior leadership experience in commercial strategy, revenue optimisation, or pricing leadership, ideally in multi-business or private-equity environments.
• Demonstrated success building and scaling high-performing commercial or pricing teams.
• Strong background in pricing science, margin management, and value-based pricing methodologies.
• Highly analytical with strong financial understanding.
• Ability to influence at executive level and work effectively across multiple business cultures.
• Experience in software, technology, or services organisations preferred

Are you passionate about turning complex data challenges into clear, scalable product solutions?
Do you enjoy leading through ambiguity, shaping roadmaps, and helping teams deliver high-quality outcomes in an evolving AI-enabled environment?
About our Team
The Enterprise Data & Analytics (EDA) team’s vision is a future where every colleague has trustworthy data they confidently use to streamline processes, drive smarter decisions and accelerate growth. We develop solutions for managing master data, provide capabilities to manage and govern data assets, and provide analytical platforms to deliver valuable business insights.
The Enterprise Product Hub (EPH) is central to that vision. EPH masters Elsevier’s saleable product data – bringing books, journals and a growing range of other products under a single governed model – and currently publishes it to around thirty consuming systems across the business. As Elsevier's product portfolio grows, so does EPH's remit, and the work ahead for the analysts, engineers and product specialists behind it.
About the Role
The Senior Data Product Manager owns a defined area of the EPH product estate – the attributes that enable us to sell a product, from what it's called to how it's identified and how it's sold. You will take your functional direction from the Head of Product Data, and will report indirectly to the Senior Director of EDA.
This role complements the existing product management by taking responsibility for a current gap in our data estate: the ingestion and publication of digital product data. As the senior regional lead, you will ensure that global standards are consistently implemented while aligning with local regulatory requirements and risk profiles. MUFG’s supportive leadership culture fosters talent development and encourages continuous improvement, making this an ideal environment for those who thrive on nurturing teams and driving excellence. • Take ownership of regional compliance oversight for Financial Crimes Compliance, Core Compliance, and Markets Compliance within a globally recognised financial institution.
• Lead a talented team in embedding global standards and methodologies while adapting to local regulatory expectations and risk profiles.

What you'll do:
As Director of Compliance Oversight – Testing, Monitoring and Issues Management at MUFG in London you will be entrusted with leading the regional execution of three critical compliance functions: monitoring routines; testing plans; and issues management. Your day-to-day responsibilities will involve collaborating closely with global function owners as well as local teams to embed global standards across EMEA while remaining responsive to local legal requirements. Your role also includes providing guidance on issue identification processes—ensuring thorough documentation; severity assessment; action planning; validation; closure—and challenging action plan adequacy when needed. Success in this position requires fostering disciplined execution among your team members; supporting talent development; coordinating transparent reporting for senior management; and maintaining open lines of communication with stakeholders across multiple jurisdictions.
• Lead the EMEA regional oversight model for compliance monitoring, testing, and issues management across multiple compliance disciplines including Financial Crimes Compliance, Core Compliance, and Markets Compliance.
• Implement global compliance standards, procedures, methodologies, and execution requirements throughout the region to ensure consistency and alignment with enterprise objectives.
• Provide senior-level regional oversight by challenging execution risks, identifying control gaps, managing overdue deliverables, and addressing quality concerns in compliance activities.
• Oversee the annual Compliance Test Plan for EMEA by managing scoping processes, ensuring execution quality, developing comprehensive reports, validating results, identifying issues, and escalating as necessary.
• Ensure testing coverage accurately reflects regional regulatory obligations, business activities, risk assessments, and global priorities to maintain robust compliance.
• Supervise regional execution of monitoring routines established by the global compliance monitoring programme to assess control effectiveness and emerging risks.
• Review monitoring results, trends, exceptions, and thematic observations to identify root cause themes and control weaknesses within the compliance framework.
• Provide regional oversight of issue identification including documentation, severity assessment, ownership assignment, action planning, validation processes, and closure protocols.
• Challenge the adequacy of action plans by evaluating milestone discipline, evidence quality, closure readiness while overseeing reporting on issue status for senior management.
• Coordinate with global function owners as well as regional compliance leadership and local teams to ensure consistency in execution while promoting transparency and accountability.
What you bring:
To excel as Director of Compliance Oversight – Testing, Monitoring and Issues Management at MUFG you will bring extensive experience from global organisations—ideally spanning over fifteen years—with significant exposure to managerial roles leading high-performing teams. Your expertise should encompass financial sector regulations including banking laws as well as supervisory guidance relevant to compliance or risk management disciplines. You will have demonstrated success implementing global operating models across diverse jurisdictions while maintaining sensitivity to local legal frameworks. Your interpersonal skills must enable you to build cooperative partnerships across regions—facilitating transparency between stakeholders at all levels. Experience with governance forums is essential along with proficiency in regulatory remediation programmes or transformation initiatives. Advanced communication capabilities are required for executive-level reporting alongside technical competence using GRC platforms or data analytics tools. Your proven ability to nurture talent within your team—combined with strategic thinking—will ensure disciplined execution of compliance functions under your leadership.
• Extensive experience working within a global organisation plus managerial experience leading teams in complex environments.
• Significant background in financial services with deep knowledge of banking laws; regulations; supervisory guidance; compliance; risk…

The Capacity Planning & Forecasting Lead is accountable for leading the development, ownership and continuous improvement of robust, data-driven capacity plans and demand forecasts across Helpdesk and Operations.
This role owns the production of accurate short, medium and long-term forecasts, the integrity of capacity models, and the delivery of insight that enables confident operational, financial and commercial decision-making. Working under the direction of the Senior Manager – Enterprise Capacity Planning & Insights, the Lead ensures supply and demand are aligned through disciplined planning, rigorous analysis, proactive stakeholder engagement and clear governance of planning assumptions.

• Lead cross-functional planning conversations with Operations, Finance, Change and senior stakeholders, ensuring plans are understood, challenged appropriately and translated into action.
4. Financial Planning & Forecasting
• Lead workforce input into budget planning, reforecasting and quarterly financial forecasts for Helpdesk & Operations, ensuring assumptions are transparent, evidence-based and operationally credible.
• Own the alignment between capacity plans, demand forecasts, service commitments and financial targets, escalating risks and trade-offs with clear recommendations.
• Deliver cost optimisation through improved resource utilisation, productivity insight, scenario modelling and clear identification of opportunities to improve commercial outcomes.
5. Change Impact & Planning Governance
• Lead capacity and demand impact assessments for business initiatives affecting Operations and Helpdesk, ensuring service, cost, FTE and commercial implications are clearly understood.
• Own the incorporation of product, process, regulatory, volume and operating model changes into forecasts and capacity plans, ensuring assumptions are documented and aligned across functions.
• Apply and strengthen capacity planning governance, ensuring planning decisions are traceable, assumptions are clear and senior stakeholders have confidence in the outputs.
• Lead best-practice adoption across planning processes, using lessons learned, performance data and stakeholder feedback to improve future planning cycles.
Key Accountabilities
• Ownership, accuracy and reliability of demand forecasts, capacity plans and planning assumptions.
• Credibility of planning outputs with Heads of Operations, Helpdesk, Finance and Change stakeholders.
• Effectiveness of variance analysis, root cause identification and corrective action planning.
• Measurable improvement in forecast accuracy, model quality and planning confidence over time.
• Alignment of capacity with service level commitments, financial targets and commercial priorities.
• Contribution to operational efficiency, cost optimisation and benefit realisation.
• Responsiveness to emerging demand trends, operational risks and changes in business priorities.
• Ownership of recovery plans when service, cost, capacity or forecast accuracy moves outside agreed business appetite.
Skills & Experience Required
Essential
• Proven experience leading capacity planning, demand forecasting or workforce planning activity within a contact centre, operations or enterprise planning environment.
• Strong understanding of workforce management and staffing methodologies.
• Strong track record of owning forecast accuracy, capacity modelling and planning governance across short, medium and long-term horizons.
• Advanced Excel skills and experience with statistical modelling techniques.
• Strong analytical and problem-solving capability with high attention to detail.
• Ability to influence cross-functional stakeholders by translating complex datasets…

Engineering

In the 12-month Software Engineering Placement, you'll gain invaluable skills by working as part of a team during part of (or multiple parts) the Development Life Cycle. Depending on your skillset and role requirements, you will develop your programming languages skills in (but not limited to) Java, C, C++, C#, Python, Raspberry Pi and/or Arduino.

Group Technical Accounting Manager
PIB Group is a fast-growing, specialist insurance intermediary and distribution consolidator. We're looking for a Group Technical Accounting Manager to lead and coordinate technical accounting matters across the Group, providing subject-matter expertise on complex accounting areas, supporting high-quality Group and holding company financial reporting, and acting as a key point of contact for auditors and advisers on technical issues. This role reports directly to the Group Head of Financial Reporting.
Location: Preferably East Midlands or London-based, but we'd welcome regional candidates who are open to travel.
What you'll be doing:
•
Own the Group's technical accounting policies (IFRS and relevant UK GAAP/Companies Act requirements), ensuring consistent application across entities, and prepare technical papers for management, auditors and the Board on complex or judgemental areas.
•
Lead acquisition accounting for business combinations (intangibles, contingent consideration, goodwill) and advise on Group restructurings, legal entity rationalisations and intra-group transfers, including common-control and capital reorganisation transactions.
•
Own the effective interest rate (EIR) models for Group debt — including debt modifications, PIK options and other complex terms — and oversee accounting for intercompany loans and balances, including alignment with Treasury systems (e.g. Kyriba) and automation of interest calculations.
•
Oversee the Group's foreign exchange accounting (functional currency assessments, translation of foreign operations, FX hedge accounting) and IFRS 16 lease models and processes, including use of CCH Tagetik or similar tools.
•
Own the accounting for share-based payment schemes under IFRS 2 (management incentive plans, options, equity/cash-settled awards), ensuring appropriate charge recognition and clear disclosure of schemes, assumptions and sensitivities.
•
Lead the Group's implementation of IFRS 18 — impact assessment, policy development and changes to primary statements and notes — and support preparation and review of Group and holding company statutory financial statements.
What we're looking for:
•
Qualified accountant (ACA/ACCA or equivalent) with strong post-qualification experience in technical accounting, ideally from a large practice (audit/technical advisory) and/or a complex, multi-entity Group environment.
•
Deep, hands-on experience in several of: business combinations and acquisition accounting; complex debt and EIR calculations; FX and consolidation of international operations; share-based payments (IFRS 2) and IFRS 16 leasing; Group restructurings and intra-group transactions.
•
Strong understanding of IFRS and UK Companies Act requirements; exposure to UK GAAP/FRC guidance is a plus.
•
Proven experience working directly with auditors and external advisers on complex transactions and models.
•
Excellent analytical skills and attention to detail, with the ability to juggle multiple complex workstreams under tight deadlines.
•
Strong communicator who can explain technical issues clearly to non-specialists, prepare concise technical papers, and collaborate across Group finance, treasury, tax, legal and local finance teams.
Why PIB Group?
PIB Group is one of the UK’s fastest-growing insurance businesses, offering real career progression, professional development, and a collaborative culture where your work truly matters.
We encourage our people to be collaborative, with entrepreneurship at our core. We are a fast-paced, growing organisation and an exciting place to be.
We also value ambition and creative thinking. You don’t have to tick every box to apply, if you bring fresh ideas and a drive to grow, we’d love to hear from you!

A well established reinsurance organisation is investing in its permanent internal data capability to meet growing demand across underwriting, operations, and finance. This is a senior, high impact role where you will help shape how data is defined, governed, and used across the enterprise.

Ipsen is a global biopharmaceutical group dedicated to improving lives and health outcomes through innovative medicines in Oncology, Neuroscience and Rare Disease.
Research and development are key elements of our strategy, reflecting our commitment to improving patients’ lives and health outcomes.
In respect to Good Manufacturing Practices and as part of the Global Clinical Supply Management department (GCSM), the Clinical Supply Chain Forecast Manager
• drive clinical supply forecasting and budgetary requirements of clinical program by providing consolidated estimates of IMPs to be produced compared to patient’s needs.
WHAT - Main Responsibilities & Technical Competencies
Clinical forecasting responsibilities
• Drive clinical supply forecasting and budgetary requirements of clinical program by providing consolidated estimates of IMPs to be produced compared to patient’s needs.
• Ensure adequate clinical forecast estimate / review is implemented for new / on-going clinical studies:
• Organize review meetings with relevant cross functional departments
• Translates into the forecasting tool the design of any new clinical study according to the study protocol as well as the recruitment projections (duration and speed of recruitment).
• Monitors closely the evolution of validated clinical study forecasts and shares them with the coordination, planning, packaging and distribution teams: analyzes deviations, decides on corrective actions, controls readjustments, reports on the progress of studies and validates milestones
• Align with clinical manufacturing team to ensure proper planning of semi-finished goods production when required.
• When clinical packaging and distribution are to be performed internally, work in tandem with clinical procurement and packaging planning manager to ensure seamless translation of the of clinical needs into production planning and take into account all the clinical studies. Main objective is on time supply to patients with no stock outs of IMP. To do so, develop, coordinate and optimize the clinical forecasts over a 3-to-12-month period
• Anticipate and assess impact on changes in clinical studies managed by the GCSM team (addition of new countries, sites, number of patients, changes in protocols, etc). Propose mitigation plans for facilitating priorisation decisions. Challenge Clinical Project Managers when relevant and consolidate the new / updated forecasts in the appropriate systems. Report on the progress of studies and validate milestones
• If needed, communicate, and follow up within CMC on the impact on the schedule to any changes observed or reported.
• IMP estimation process:
• Coordinate and lead meetings for new clinical studies (IMP kick off meeting & IMP estimation meeting) involving relevant stakeholders to ensure on time engagement of each team members.
• Ensure proper IMP risk assessment is implemented and maintained for each clinical study, including but not limited to risks linked to stock out, distribution strategies, complexity of the study.
• Transversal management responsibilities
• Coordinate with team members in a matrix environment
Continuous improvement responsibilities
• Lead change management initiatives with cross functional teams both internally and externally to Ipsen
• Quality:
• Perform its activities according to Ipsen Quality Management System
• Contribute to the performance of the site supporting the compliance of KPIs (First Time Quality, On time CAPA closed)
• Continuous improvement, QEHS and CSR:
• Contribute to continuous improvement projects within the Global Clinical Supply Management Department and/or wider Pharmaceutical Development.
• Be a promoter of continuous improvement processes and to guarantee the method,
• Respect and ensure respect for applicable good practices (GMP, GMPD, etc.) and Environmental, Health and Safety rules through the procedures in force within the establishment,
• Drive and implement actions to develop CSR within the framework of Ipsen's orientations.
QEEHS Responsibilities:
• To respect the applicable good practices (BPF, BPD, ...), the rules Energy Environment Health and Safety through the procedures in force within the establishment.
CSR Responsibilities:
• To apply and make proposals within the framework of Ipsen's guidelines for actions aimed at developing CSR.
HOW - Behavioural Competencies Required
Excellence in execution
• Approaches priority setting and setting the stage through the lens of execution
• Establishes clarity about the goals, accountabilities, timelines, and next steps; can identify/spot opportunities for real impact on patient and society
• Able to be focused and performance-driven with clear KPIs
• Plans and aligns effectively (steps, timelines etc.)
• Displays a commitment to best practice sharing and setting
• Promotes single point of accountabilities
Ensures Accountability
• Ensures single accountable referents per task/project/outcome (independent of organizational context or multi-team projects)
• Builds and anchors an environment where people have the skills and habits to ask for clarification when accountabilities are unclear
• Consults/seeks relevant stakeholder views/expertise and coaches/ensures decisions are made by consent vs. consensus
• Takes personal accountability for decisions, risk, actions, successes and failures, and fosters the same for others

Job Description:
About the Role
Epiq Advisory for Law Firms is seeking a Forward Deployed Legal Engineer to help law firm clients redesign legal work through practical process improvement and AI-enabled workflows. This is a hands-on, client-facing role for someone who understands how lawyers work, can diagnose inefficient processes, and can translate legal needs into usable AI agents, automations, and workflow solutions. The ideal candidate will have a JD or comparable legal training, strong legal-domain fluency, and hands-on experience creating AI agents and working with large language models in applied legal or professional services settings.
This role works closely with the AI Enablement team and intersects with Epiq Advisory’s Data Modernization, Document Management, Knowledge Advisory, and Change Enablement teams. It requires the ability to work directly with lawyers, knowledge professionals, legal operations teams, and technical delivery partners to identify high-value use cases, design agentic workflows, document requirements, test outputs, and guide adoption. The Forward Deployed Legal Engineer will help clients move from AI experimentation to practical, governed, workflow-aligned use cases that deliver measurable value.
Key Responsibilities
Legal Workflow Design & AI Agent Enablement
• Work directly with law firm clients and Epiq Advisory teams to understand legal workflows, pain points, handoffs, and goals, then translate them into practical process improvements and AI-enabled solutions.
• Identify, prioritize, and document legal AI use cases
• Create, configure, and refine LLM-based workflows, AI agents, prompts, evaluation criteria, and human-in-the-loop review steps tailored to legal work.
• Work hands-on with large language models, agent frameworks, retrieval patterns, and legal workflow context to turn concepts into usable prototypes and delivery-ready designs.
• Partner with AI Enablement and technical resources to define requirements, data inputs, integrations, permissions, and workflow logic without needing to personally write production code.
• Prototype concepts using available AI, automation, and no-code or low-code tools, gather feedback from users, and help convert the strongest ideas into client-ready solutions.
• Map current-state and future-state workflows, identify bottlenecks, and recommend process changes that make AI adoption practical, defensible, and measurable.
• Coordinate across Data Modernization, Document Management, Knowledge Advisory, and Change Enablement workstreams so AI agents are grounded in trusted content, aligned to system realities, and supported by effective adoption plans.
Legal-Centric Problem Solving
• Partner with lawyers, paralegals, knowledge professionals, and legal operations teams to surface the real problem behind the stated request.
• Apply legal training and legal-domain understanding to design workflows that fit how legal work actually gets done.
• Establish evaluation criteria and quality benchmarks appropriate to legal contexts, where accuracy, defensibility, and explainability matter.
• Define and track adoption, usage, and value-realization metrics tied directly to client outcomes.
Security, Confidentiality & Governance
• Work with the Data Modernization team to align AI agents and workflows with secure data foundations, trusted knowledge sources, confidentiality requirements, and privacy expectations for privileged legal information.
• Design solutions that respect client governance, data-residency, retention, and access-control requirements.
• Collaborate with Document Management and Knowledge Advisory teams to connect AI use cases to firm content, document repositories, metadata, search, retrieval, and knowledge governance.
• Document architecture, data flows, and decisions to support client security review, audit, and risk management.
Practice Development & Growth

The role acts as the interface between project delivery teams, design consultants, contractors, asset owners, operations teams, and digital delivery functions, ensuring that information and asset data requirements are met in accordance with organisational standards, client requirements, and industry best practice.A key objective of the role is to ensure that accurate, complete, and structured information is delivered to support operational readiness, maintenance and asset management.
This role is ideal for a collaborative and detail-oriented professional with the ability to work effectively in a specialised technical environment. The successful candidate will be organised, thorough, and resilient, with the ability to manage complex challenges and deliver tasks to completion. A strong focus on accuracy, quality, and compliance with established standards is essential, as is a commitment to minimising errors. Responsibilities include researching and analysing information, working with multiple platforms, and following technical specifications. • Providing document control support for UK & Ireland projects
• Facilitating document review processes. Managing document release processes to client databases.
• Establish and manage Common Data Environment (CDE) requirements across projects
• Ensure compliance with organisational information management standards and project information requirements

• Monitor the quality, completeness, and accuracy of project information deliverables

• Providing first line support to Project Execution team members in the use of information management tooling
• Define asset information requirements in collaboration with asset owners and operational stakeholders.
• Ensure asset data is captured, validated, and structured throughout project delivery
• Coordinate the integration of engineering, operational, and asset management data into the applicable systems.
• Manage asset information handover processes, ensuring all required deliverables are complete and verified.

Our Professional Services team partners closely with customers to deliver complex, business-critical deployment and installation projects. Working in a fast-paced, technology-led environment, we focus on delivering exceptional customer experiences through strong project governance, collaboration and operational excellence.
We are looking for an experienced Senior Project Manager to join our growing Professional Services organisation. This customer-facing role focuses on managing the deployment and installation of our solutions, coordinating customer stakeholders and internal delivery teams from project initiation through to completion. The role is dedicated to customer delivery, rather than internal business projects.
Technical understanding is essential, particularly in cyber security or networking. You will need to engage confidently with customer technical teams, understand deployment requirements and dependencies, and translate technical considerations into clear project plans. What Will I Be Doing?
As a Senior Project Manager, you will lead complex customer deployment and installation projects throughout the full project lifecycle, ensuring delivery against agreed timelines, budgets, scope and customer objectives while maintaining strong stakeholder engagement and governance standards.
In this role, you will:
• Lead end-to-end delivery of customer deployment and installation projects, developing project plans and managing schedules, resources, budgets and cross-functional dependencies while ensuring compliance with governance requirements and lifecycle gates.
• Work closely with customer technical teams and internal delivery specialists to understand customer environments, installation prerequisites and technical dependencies, incorporating these into project planning and delivery.
• Manage project risks, issues, scope, financials and change requests, proactively implementing mitigation strategies to support successful customer outcomes.
• Use your technical understanding to identify deployment risks, facilitate technical discussions and coordinate the resolution of issues with the appropriate specialists.
• Maintain effective communication with customers and internal delivery teams through executive reporting, project dashboards and regular status updates, ensuring alignment across customer, business and technical stakeholders.
• Define and measure project success against agreed customer objectives and key performance indicators, using data to inform decisions and assess delivery performance.
• Support collaborative project teams by coordinating activities, resolving delivery challenges and maintaining positive customer and stakeholder relationships.
• Continuously improve customer deployment and installation delivery by refining project methodologies, sharing lessons learned and supporting consistent project management practices within Professional Services.
What Do I Need?
We are looking for someone who combines strong project delivery experience with technical understanding of cyber security or networking, alongside effective communication, stakeholder management and problem-solving skills.
• 5+ years of project management experience, ideally within Professional Services, SaaS, cyber security or another technology-focused environment.
• Proven experience delivering complex customer-facing deployment or installation projects involving cross-functional teams, multiple stakeholders and competing priorities.
• A sound understanding of cyber security or networking concepts, gained through technical experience or managing relevant deployments, with the ability to understand how customer environments affect installation and delivery.
• Confidence discussing technical requirements, dependencies and risks with customer IT, networking or security teams and internal technical specialists.
• Strong expertise in project governance, risk management, budgeting, forecasting, resource planning and project controls.
• Demonstrated ability to engage and influence senior customer and internal delivery stakeholders, maintaining alignment and accountability throughout delivery.
• Strong communication, leadership, organisational and problem-solving skills, including the ability to explain technical delivery considerations clearly to non-technical stakeholders.
• Experience improving customer project delivery processes and embedding project management best practices.

Purpose of the role
The Senior Assistant Company Secretary will support the Company Secretary in delivering effective corporate governance and company secretarial services across the Group, with primary responsibility for the Group’s Insurance businesses and its regulated entities.
Reporting to the Company Secretary, the Senior Assistant will act as the lead company secretarial adviser for the Insurance division, overseeing the delivery of effective governance and secretariat support to its Boards and Committees. The role will ensure compliance with applicable legal, regulatory and governance requirements, whilst promoting high standards of corporate governance within a complex regulated environment.
In addition to supporting the Insurance division, the Senior Assistant will assist the Company Secretary on wider Group governance matters, strategic initiatives and governance projects.
The Senior Assistant Company Secretary will provide leadership, guidance and line management to junior members of the Governance team and act as a trusted adviser to senior stakeholders across the Insurance businesses and wider Group.
This role plays a key part in maintaining a strong governance culture across the regulated insurance entities and Group, supporting effective decision-making, regulatory compliance and robust governance arrangements that are aligned with the Group's strategic objectives.
Key Responsibilities
Governance and Compliance
•        Act as the lead company secretarial adviser for the Group's Insurance businesses and regulated entities, while supporting the Company Secretary on wider Group governance.
•        Provide advice and ensure compliance with the Companies Act 2006, applicable insurance regulatory requirements, regulations and corporate governance codes (e.g., The Wates Principles).
•        Assist in the development, implementation, and monitoring of governance frameworks and policies for both the Insurance division and wider Group.
•        Monitor governance and regulatory developments and advise on their impact.
•        Promote effective governance practices across the Group's subsidiaries, supporting directors in understanding their duties and responsibilities.
Board and Committee Support
•        Act as the primary governance support for the Insurance Boards and their Committees, ensuring effective operation and compliance with applicable legal, regulatory and governance requirements.
•        Manage ownership of end-to-end Board and Committee cycles for the Insurance division and support other Boards and Committees within the Group as required.
•        Support the establishment and ongoing development of governance structures, including Terms of Reference, annual work plans, delegated authorities and governance processes.
•        Support the establishment and operationalisation of new Boards and Committees.
•        Manage written resolutions and approvals outside the formal meeting cycle.
•        Advise directors and committee members on governance matters, Board procedures and effective decision-making.
•        Support Board effectiveness reviews, director inductions and ongoing director development across both the Insurance division and wider Group.
Stakeholder Management
•        Build and maintain strong relationships with Board members, senior executives, and external advisers across the Insurance businesses and wider Group.
•        Working with cross-functional teams including Insurance, Legal, Finance, Controllership, Treasury and Tax to deliver projects.
•        Act as a key liaison between Boards and senior management, ensuring clear communication and alignment.
•        Act as a primary point of contact with overseas company secretarial providers, ensuring timely coordination, accurate governance support and consistency of standards across all jurisdictions.
•        Support the operation and ongoing development of the Group’s Delegation of Authority Framework.
Statutory Activities
•        Provide governance support for the annual report and accounts process for the Group and its subsidiaries, including governance disclosures, Board approvals and related documentation.
Line Management and Team Development

Project Support and Governance Initiatives

•        Contribute to strategic governance reviews and governance enhancement initiatives across the Group.

• Demonstrable familiarity with surveillance systems such as Nasdaq SMARTS

Joining Moderna means advancing mRNA science to transform medicine. Work with exceptional global teams on a broad pipeline and build a career that makes a real difference for patients.

This long term investment will create skilled jobs and strengthen collaboration with academic, NHS, and government partners. We welcome experts ready to help expand access to life saving vaccines.
At Moderna's Harwell manufacturing facility, you will play a critical role in ensuring the quality, integrity, and stability of materials and products supporting our mRNA manufacturing operations. Reporting to the Associate Director, Quality Control, you will combine hands-on analytical chemistry expertise with the coordination and execution of GMP stability programs, using advanced analytical technologies, laboratory information systems, and scientific data analysis to support manufacturing, product release, and regulatory compliance. This is an opportunity to contribute to global stability programs, strengthen analytical excellence, and explore emerging digital and Generative AI-enabled technologies within a highly regulated, science-driven environment.

Maintain accurate and current stability databases, inventory records, and supporting documentation to ensure complete sample and data traceability.
• Perform scientific data trending and statistical analysis: Analyse stability testing results to identify trends, evaluate product performance over time, and support scientific assessment of stability data. Maintain up-to-date stability tables, charts, and statistical analyses across ongoing studies, contributing to data-driven quality and regulatory decisions.
• Develop stability protocols, technical reports, and regulatory documentation: Create, review, revise, and approve stability protocols and reports within the scope of assigned responsibilities. Contribute to the preparation and review of stability-related sections for regulatory submissions, ensuring scientific accuracy, data integrity, and alignment with current regulatory requirements.
• Coordinate external laboratory testing and data management: Organise and execute stability sample shipments to external testing laboratories, supporting appropriate sample tracking and documentation. Request, retrieve, and review stability testing data and reports from external vendors and shared repositories, ensuring internal stability binders, databases, and study records remain accurate and complete.
• Maintain laboratory operational readiness: Perform essential laboratory support activities, including reagent preparation, sample management, routine equipment maintenance, laboratory housekeeping, and the ordering, stocking, and management of QC consumables and supplies. Help maintain a safe, organised, and inspection-ready laboratory environment.
• Support analytical troubleshooting and technical development: Assist with investigations into analytical assay performance, method-related issues, and laboratory equipment problems. Share technical knowledge with colleagues and support more junior laboratory staff through data review, training, and troubleshooting activities.
• Contribute to quality investigations and continuous improvement: Participate in the preparation and execution of quality system records, including investigations, deviations, change controls, and Corrective and Preventive Actions (CAPAs). Author and revise SOPs, technical protocols, and reports while identifying opportunities to improve laboratory workflows, analytical reliability, and stability program execution.
• Uphold GMP compliance and data integrity: Execute laboratory and stability activities in accordance with applicable GxP regulations, internal policies, SOPs, and work instructions. Apply Good Documentation Practices and data integrity principles to ensure analytical results, electronic records, and supporting documentation are accurate, complete, traceable, and readily available for regulatory audits and inspections.

Job Description:
Your impact
Are you ready to make an impact and gain hands-on experience working on real-world projects from day one?
At Leonardo, we’re looking for industrial placement students who want to be part of something extraordinary—shaping innovation, advancing technology, and enhancing global safety.
Our placements are designed to help you apply your studies in a practical setting, develop your technical skills, and gain valuable insight into how our business operates.
Our Industrial Placement Programme
Our Programme offers you the chance to spend a year with us, working on meaningful projects alongside subject matter experts, within multidisciplinary teams, and across the product lifecycle. You’ll receive a salary of £26,228, with coaching and support from a dedicated team to help you achieve both your placement objectives and personal development goals.

During your placement, we encourage you to spend at least three days each week on site to integrate with your team and maximise your learning experience.
What you will do as an Industrial Placement Electronics Engineer
You will support the design and development of our world leading electro-optical, communications and information system products under the guidance of experienced Electronics Engineering Leads.
You will be introduced to utilising state-of-the-art methods, technology and tools to explore all aspects of the development lifecycle, including requirements analysis, design, implementation, test, acceptance and product support.
You will interface with customers (internal and external) on many factors within the design and liaise closely with Engineers from all other disciplines including Mechanical, Software, Systems, Supportability and Design Integrity. Electronics Engineers design, document, build and test electronics circuits and firmware designs to go into our various systems.
In Electronics Engineering, you might be involved in designing for mixed signal design, power supply design, DAC/ADC, FPGA, high-speed serial interfaces and video/communication processing algorithms. The opportunity will be there to engage with all of these technologies across a diverse, interesting and exciting range of  products including Thermal Imaging Cameras, Vehicle Camera systems, Counter UAV systems, Electronic Warfare products and Communication Systems.
There will be opportunities to develop expertise in the design of circuits, FPGAs and subsystems at various stages in the product lifecycle. Qualifications

Security Clearance
Many of our roles are subject to security and export control restrictions set by UK Government Security requirements and customer obligations.  As a result, and in line with the UK Government Baseline Personnel Security Standard (BPSS) requirements, all successful applicants will be asked to provide evidence of identity, eligibility to work in the UK, criminal record declaration information and employment and/or education history verification for the previous five years.
For staff operating in more sensitive posts, there is an additional range of personnel security controls referred to as National Security Vetting (NSV).  As part of this process, a range of factors may be considered, including an individual's background, travel history, nationality, previous nationalities held and other information relevant to the vetting assessment.
To be eligible for National Security Vetting at SC level, applicants will generally be expected to have continuously resided in the UK for the previous five years. For DV clearance, this is typically ten years.  In some circumstances, time spent overseas may be accepted, with additional overseas checks.  Additional vetting requirements may apply upon appointment.

Job Description: Equipment Engineer Wafer Fab and Epitaxy (Continental Shift)
Location: Caswell, Northamptonshire
Reports to: Equipment Engineering Shift Manager
About Lumentum
Lumentum (NASDAQ: LITE) is a global leader in innovative optical and photonic products enabling optical networking and commercial laser customers worldwide. Our technologies are integral to virtually every type of telecom, enterprise, and data centre network, and support advanced manufacturing and next generation sensing applications. Lumentum’s UK wafer fabrication facility in Caswell is a centre of excellence for high-performance optoelectronic devices used in telecommunications and industrial systems.
Role Summary
As an Equipment Technician, you will provide technical support for the operation and maintenance of wafer fabrication and epitaxy equipment on a continental shift pattern. This role offers the opportunity to work on advanced III-V semiconductor technologies within a highly specialised UK fabrication facility, supporting products deployed globally in next-generation communications networks. Your primary focus will be the fault diagnosis, repair, and optimisation of advanced semiconductor process tools including vacuum, pneumatic, mechanical, electrical, and RF systems, as well as equipment handling hazardous process gases and chemicals.
This is a hands-on, high-precision engineering role ideal for those with experience maintaining complex electro-mechanical systems in critical environments including high-tech manufacturing, aerospace, defence, or UK Armed Forces technical trades.
Key Responsibilities
• Provide rapid first-line engineering response to minimise tool downtime and production impact.
• Conduct repairs, fault diagnosis and preventative maintenance on semiconductor processing equipment including, but not limited to lithography, etch, PVD, PECVD and MOVPE reactor systems.
• Manage chemical and specialty gas supply systems in compliance with statutory, site safety and environmental standards.
• Support maintenance of gas delivery, exhaust and abatement systems associated with epitaxy and PECVD tools.
• Manage spare parts inventory to ensure availability of critical components and minimise downtime.
• Implement and support preventative maintenance strategies to maximise OEE (Overall Equipment Effectiveness) and uptime.
• Contribute to continuous improvement initiatives (Kaizen, 6S, 8D) and maintain accurate documentation of actions and outcomes.
• Participate in production and planning meetings to represent equipment engineering performance.
• Support the site emergency response function including participation in the Site Emergency Response Team.
• Fork-lift truck operation will be required (training will be provided).
Key Relationships
• Process and Equipment Engineering Teams
• Facilities and Maintenance Teams
• Manufacturing Operations Team
• MES (PROMIS) and IT Teams
Qualifications
Apprenticeship, HNC, HND or Degree in an Electrical or Mechanical Engineering discipline (or equivalent). Alternatively, a minimum of 5 years’ directly relevant experience in complex electro-mechanical system maintenance.
Preferred Backgrounds and Transferable Skills
We actively welcome applications from engineers with experience in high-reliability environments such as aerospace, defence, automotive manufacturing, pharmaceuticals, oil & gas, power generation, or UK Armed Forces technical trades. Direct semiconductor experience is advantageous but not essential.
Skills
Essential:
• Proven experience in a high-tech, precision-engineering environment.
• Strong fault-finding and diagnostic ability across electrical, electronic and mechanical systems.
• Ability to work safely with hazardous gases and chemicals.
• Ability to follow detailed documented procedures with minimal supervision.
• Competence in documenting procedures, risk assessments, and method statements.
• Effective time management and organisational skills.
• Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications.
• Team-oriented approach with excellent communication skills.
• Ability to read and interpret technical documentation and communicate effectively within a safety-critical manufacturing environment.
Desirable:
• Previous experience within a semiconductor or cleanroom manufacturing environment.
Other Requirements
• 40.3 hours per week on a continental shift pattern (2 days, 2 nights, 4 off), 12-hour shifts including weekends and bank holidays as part of the continental rotation.
• Work is performed within a cleanroom environment (cleanroom garments provided).
• Role requires use of Self-Contained Breathing Apparatus (SCBA). Candidates must be able to meet the medical and respiratory protective equipment (RPE) face-fit requirements associated with SCBA use in accordance with site safety standards.
• Must be eligible to work in the UK.

markelcorp.wd5.myworkdayjobs.com/globalc.description_excerpt:
Are you looking for a career where you can make a real impact?
At Markel, we believe what we do matters. Insurance is more than a policy; it's a promise that enables individuals and businesses to move forward with confidence. We are proud of our people-first culture, our entrepreneurial approach, and our commitment to finding solutions to complex risks.
As we continue to grow, we are looking for an Underwriting Risk Analyst to join our Underwriting Strategy & Performance (USP) team. This is an exciting opportunity to work at the centre of underwriting decision-making, helping shape risk appetite, identify emerging exposures, and support profitable portfolio growth across Markel International.
What part will you play? If you’re looking for a place where you can make a meaningful difference, you’ve found it. The work we do at Markel gives people the confidence to move forward and seize opportunities, and you’ll find your fit amongst our global community of optimists and problem-solvers. We’re always pushing each other to go further because we believe that when we realize our potential, we can help others reach theirs.
Join us and play your part in something special!
The opportunity:
The Underwriting Strategy & Performance (USP) team exists to enable profitable underwriting by supporting strong decision-making, portfolio optimisation and effective governance. We work in partnership with underwriting teams and business leaders to provide insight, challenge and oversight.
Our team brings together expertise across underwriting performance, underwriting risk, technical underwriting, wordings, reinsurance and underwriting oversight.
The Underwriting Risk Analyst will support the development, monitoring and management of underwriting risk across Markel International. Working closely with underwriting, actuarial, exposure management, reinsurance and enterprise risk teams, you will provide insight and analysis that helps the business understand and manage volatility, accumulation risk and emerging threats.
This role offers a unique opportunity to gain exposure to a broad range of insurance classes and strategic underwriting decisions while contributing to the continued development of Markel's underwriting risk framework.
What you’ll be doing:
• Support the Head of Underwriting Risk and the International CUO develop and own the company’s appetite for volatility around the business plan combined ratio.
• Provide analysis and reporting to help identify sources of such volatility, including natural and non-natural perils and emerging risks.
• Monitor portfolio trends and risk indicators, highlighting areas requiring management attention and support live event response reporting.
• Develop scenarios, stress tests and risk assessments to support underwriting decision-making.
• Prepare analysis and materials for the Underwriting Risk Group and related governance forums.
• Work collaboratively with Exposure Management, Actuarial, Risk Management, Reinsurance and Underwriting teams.
• Be aware of, and provide analysis on, the specific and systemic risks to Markel International's product portfolio including the impact of external political, economic, social and technological trends that may affect levels of risk.
• Promote a culture of risk awareness and transparent reporting across underwriting divisions.
• Continuously improve Markel’s best practices in underwriting risk management, using developments both within and outside the insurance industry
Our must-haves:
• We are looking for someone who is curious, analytical and passionate about understanding risk.
• Strong analytical, problem-solving and organisational skills.
• The ability to work independently on complex analysis while managing multiple priorities.
• Excellent communication and stakeholder management.
• Advanced Microsoft Office skills and experience using reporting, analytics or business intelligence tools.
• Knowledge of catastrophe modelling, exposure management or broader underwriting risk tools, techniques and best practices.
• A sound understanding of insurance and reinsurance principles.
• Progress towards, or interest in pursuing, relevant insurance or risk management qualifications would be beneficial, though not essential. Study support may be available.
Who we are:
Markel Group (NYSE – MKL) a Fortune 500 company with over 60 offices in 20+ countries, is a holding company for insurance, reinsurance, specialist advisory, and investment operations around the world.
We’re all about people | We win together | We strive for better | We enjoy the everyday | We think further
What’s in it for you?
• A great starting salary plus annual bonus & strong benefits package.
• 25 days paid holiday plus Bank Holidays, with the opportunity to buy/sell extra leave
• Fantastic company pension scheme, private medical and dental cover, life assurance, travel insurance cover, income protection, season ticket loan as well as other great benefits on offer
• There are countless opportunities to learn new skills and develop in your career and we can provide the support needed to do just that!
Are you ready to play your part?
Choose ‘Apply Now’ to fill out our short application, so that we can find out more about you.
Markel celebrates the value of a diverse workforce that brings experience and expertise from a wide variety of backgrounds and life circumstances. Whatever your background, if you feel you meet the requirements of this role then we want to hear from you. We are also happy to consider candidates who are looking for flexible working patterns.
We are an equal opportunity employer and value diversity at our company. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, colour, national origin, sex, gender, gender expression, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, or disability status.
We will ensure that individuals with disabilities are provided with all reasonable accommodations to be able to participate in the job application or interview process and to perform essential job functions if successful. Please contact us via email at rec@markel.com or call us at 0161 507 5827 to request any accommodations that may be needed. This includes any alternative formats of any documents or information on how to apply offline.
